compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:268:                <div class="card-desc">~50 new bash <code>DANGEROUS_PATTERNS</code> covering cloud destructive subcommands (AWS/GCP/Azure/PaaS/IaC/orchestration), git destructive (remote-branch del, <code>branch -D</code>, <code>tag -d</code>, <code>reflog expire</code>, <code>restore .</code>), storage tools (<code>lvremove</code>, <code>mkfs</code>, <code>dd of=/dev/</code>, <code>zfs destroy</code>, <code>cryptsetup luksClose</code>), persistence (<code>crontab -r</code>, <code>systemctl disable/stop</code>, <code>pm2 delete</code>), DB CLI inline (<code>DROP/TRUNCATE/DELETE FROM/FLUSHALL/SHUTDOWN</code>), system-path overwrite, perm lockout, <code>curl|sh</code>. ~12 new <code>DANGEROUS_PYTHON</code> patterns (<code>cursor.execute DROP</code>, SQLAlchemy <code>drop_all</code>, Mongo <code>dropDatabase/deleteMany</code>, Redis <code>flushall</code>, <code>os.unlink</code>/<code>shutil.rmtree</code> on system paths). <strong>HIGH_RISK_TOOLS = {bash, python_exec, task, web_fetch}</strong> excluded from Always-Approve UI shortcut — even with auto-approve on, these still prompt; the "Always Approve" button is hidden for them, so there's no UI path to a permanent bypass. Cross-surface: same denylist mirrored into <code>~/.claude/hooks/pre-bash-safety.sh</code> + Learning_Factory source-of-truth.</div>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:476:    <div class="explain">The Compactor implements a two-stage strategy borrowed from OpenCode: first prune old tool outputs (cheap, no API call), then if still over threshold, generate an LLM summary (costs one API call). Protected tools (todo, semantic_search) are never pruned. The File Cache uses LRU eviction with mtime validation to prevent stale reads.</div>

compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1137:        <strong>semantic_search</strong> &mdash; Searches your codebase by <em>meaning</em>, not just keywords. If you search "authentication logic", it finds code related to login/auth even if those exact words aren't used. Uses AWS Titan embeddings to convert code into vectors, then finds the most similar chunks. Python files are split by function/class (AST-aware), so results are more meaningful than line-based search.<br><br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1138:        <strong>web_fetch</strong> &mdash; Fetches a URL and converts the HTML to readable text. Protected against SSRF attacks: blocks requests to private IPs (10.x, 192.168.x, 127.0.0.1), blocks redirects to internal servers, limits response to 2MB. Useful for reading documentation or API specs from the web.
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1140:    <div class="explain"><strong>semantic_search</strong> uses Titan Embed v2 to vectorize code chunks, then cosine similarity to find matches by meaning rather than exact text. Requires an explicit <code>action="index"</code> call first (costs ~$0.01). In practice, <code>grep</code> handles 95% of search needs &mdash; semantic search is for cases where keyword matching fails. <strong>view_image</strong> base64-encodes the image and injects it as a content block into the next Claude API call for multimodal analysis.</div>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1155:        <strong>ask_user</strong> &mdash; Pauses the agent and asks you a question. Shows a text input with Submit/Skip buttons. The agent waits up to 5 minutes for your response, then continues based on your answer. Used when the agent needs clarification before proceeding.
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1157:    <div class="explain"><strong>Skills</strong> are injected into the system prompt at runtime, extending the agent's behavior without code changes. <strong>Sub-agents</strong> run as child sessions with scoped tool access and independent context, enabling parallel delegation. <strong>ask_user</strong> implements a blocking prompt with a 5-minute timeout, using threading.Event for synchronization between the agent thread and the UI thread.</div>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1164:        <strong>todo_write</strong> &mdash; Creates or updates a task list. Each task has a name, status (pending/in_progress/completed), and an active description. The agent uses this to plan multi-step work and track progress. The todo list persists with the session, so it survives across messages.<br><br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1165:        <strong>todo_read</strong> &mdash; Reads the current task list to check what's been done and what's remaining. The agent uses this to maintain awareness of its progress on complex tasks.<br><br>

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-b-iter1.md:5292:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3592:.\_archive\compact_v3\ship\chat.ipynb:35:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Action | How |\n|--------|-----|\n| **Send message** | Type in input box, press Send |\n| **Stop agent** | Click Stop button |\n| **Check cost** | Type `/cost` |\n| **Code review** | Type `/review filename.py` |\n| **Explain code** | Type `/explain filename.py` |\n| **Generate tests** | Type `/test filename.py` |\n| **Verify project** | Type `/verify` |\n| **Apply standards** | Type `/standards filename.py` |\n| **Revert file** | Type `/revert filename.py` or `/revert all` |\n| **Compact context** | Click Compact button (or auto at 80%) |\n| **Clean traces** | Click Clean button (removes audit/snapshots, keeps sessions) |\n| **Save/Load** | Save button (auto-saves each message) / Session dropdown + Load |\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\n| Task | What to type |\n|------|-------------|\n| Read a file | \"Read app.py\" |\n| Find files | \"Find all Python files in this project\" |\n| Fix a bug | \"Read app.py, find the bug, and fix it\" |\n| Create chart | \"Create a bar chart from sales.csv showing revenue by product\" |\n| Create report | \"Create a Word report summarizing the data in results.csv\" |\n| Run command | \"Run git status\" |\n| Analyze image | \"Look at screenshot.png and describe what you see\" |\n| Search code | \"Find where authentication is handled in this codebase\" |\n\n## 22 Tools\n\n| Category | Tools | Approval? |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. Context auto-compacts at 80% usage (prune old tool outputs, then LLM summarize if needed)\n\n## Token Overhead Per API Call\n\n| Component | Tokens |\n|-----------|--------|\n| System prompt | ~1,200 |\n| Tool schemas | ~1,800 (lazy-load: ~1,200 for coding tasks) |\n| Bedrock overhead | ~346 |\n| **Total per call** | **~3,350** |\n\n## Session Management\n\n| Feature | How |\n|---------|-----|\n| **Auto-save** | Every message auto-saves (messages, todos, metadata) |\n| **Load session** | Session dropdown + Load button |\n| **New session** | New button (clears all state) |\n| **Checkpoints** | `/checkpoint name` (saves snapshot, max 50) |\n\n## Commands vs Skills\n\n| Method | How | Depth | Persists? |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. Commands cover the same categories with less detail.\n\n## Config\n\nDefault config is set in Cell 3 (before launch). Change model, temperature, thinking mode anytime in the chatbot UI during use.\n\nKey security settings (Cell 3):\n- `aws_bedrock_only = True` \u2014 blocks all AWS except Bedrock\n- `session_cost_limit = 1.0` \u2014 max $1 per session\n- `require_tool_approval = True` \u2014 approve/deny before execution"
compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-b-iter1.md:5294:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4429:.\_archive\compact_v3\MAIN\agent\chat.ipynb:35:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Action | How |\n|--------|-----|\n| **Send message** | Type in input box, press Send |\n| **Stop agent** | Click Stop button |\n| **Check cost** | Type `/cost` |\n| **Code review** | Type `/review filename.py` |\n| **Explain code** | Type `/explain filename.py` |\n| **Generate tests** | Type `/test filename.py` |\n| **Verify project** | Type `/verify` |\n| **Apply standards** | Type `/standards filename.py` |\n| **Revert file** | Type `/revert filename.py` or `/revert all` |\n| **Compact context** | Click Compact button (or auto at 80%) |\n| **Clean traces** | Click Clean button (removes audit/snapshots, keeps sessions) |\n| **Save/Load** | Save button (auto-saves each message) / Session dropdown + Load |\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\n| Task | What to type |\n|------|-------------|\n| Read a file | \"Read app.py\" |\n| Find files | \"Find all Python files in this project\" |\n| Fix a bug | \"Read app.py, find the bug, and fix it\" |\n| Create chart | \"Create a bar chart from sales.csv showing revenue by product\" |\n| Create report | \"Create a Word report summarizing the data in results.csv\" |\n| Run command | \"Run git status\" |\n| Analyze image | \"Look at screenshot.png and describe what you see\" |\n| Search code | \"Find where authentication is handled in this codebase\" |\n\n## 22 Tools\n\n| Category | Tools | Approval? |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-g-iter1.md:3122:compact_v5/_phase_2\v4_reference\chat.ipynb:6:   "source": "# SageAgent V4.10.10\n\n**Setup:** Run cells 1-3 in order:\n- **Cell 1** installs packages (run once per kernel).\n- **Cell 2** shows config widgets — set Model, Temperature, Workspace, Mock-Mode, and the **Bedrock-only** checkbox (default ticked = strict; untick to allow S3 / Textract / Lambda / DynamoDB writes with approval).\n- **Cell 3** reads all widget values into `CONFIG` and launches the agent. The \"Configuration Applied\" banner displays the chosen AWS scope.\n\n**Core files:** `sagemaker_agent.py` (the entire agent) + this notebook + `memory.md` (auto-populated) + `AGENT_STATUS.md` (long-running handoff) + `skills/` (10 skills + `/reflexion`).\n\n**v4.9 highlights** (full notes in `changelogs/CHANGELOG_v4.9.X.md`):\n- v4.9.0 — `auto_trigger: false` honoured; word-boundary keyword match; SYSTEM_PROMPT critique-handling section\n- v4.9.1 — `/unskill <name>` + sticky deactivation\n- v4.9.2 — minimum-ship zip\n- v4.9.3 — prompt-injection scanner; CSO description validator; `/reflexion` skill\n- v4.9.4 — IterationBudget shared parent+sub-agents; ErrorClassifier + jittered backoff; pre-compact tool-result pruning; opt-in auxiliary-model compaction (Haiku); structured Resolved/Pending Questions in summary\n- v4.9.5 — opt-in self-patching skills (agent proposes SKILL.md improvements, you review via `/skill suggestions` then `/skill apply <name>`)\n- v4.9.6 — production hardening: no default skill auto-load, Bedrock-safe compact history, fixed build worktree isolation, dirty-state worktree overlay, serialized parallel builds, durable status doc, local-git-only SageMaker policy\n- v4.9.7 — `/context` diagnostic: context percentage, top tool-output sources, duplicate file reads, suggested action\n- v4.10.0 — Runnable parity (5 phases): notebook_edit (surgical .ipynb cell editor), skill listing token budget cap, per-sub-agent env-details, model-aware context window auto-derive, reactive compact on Bedrock CONTEXT_OVERFLOW. 5 Codex per-phase reviews, 9 correctness issues caught and fixed.\n- v4.10.1 — same-day follow-up: segment-level Context Collapse (collapses 3+ stale tool round-trips into one synthetic Bedrock-safe pair) + default model switched to Sonnet 4.5 (cache activates from 1024 tokens vs Haiku 4096).\n- v4.10.2 — verify-contract softened: now SUGGEST /verify after 3+ logic edits and wait for user confirm; strict mode opt-in via CONFIG.enforce_verify_contract=True (Codex caught the prompt contradiction)\n- v4.10.3 — production-readiness review apply: ship-gate verifier (verify_ship_zip.py), cache-boundary regression test (6 tests), many-skill stress test (100/1000 skills), clearer permission denials\n- v4.10.4 — sub-agent work-context handoff (bounded AGENT_STATUS slice + active todos + last 10 changed files), Codex follow-up review fix\n- v4.10.5 — Learning_Factory pattern adoption: post-compact resume protocol + structured summary sections (#12 Standing Constraints + #13 Critical Don't-Forget) + skill self-patching 4-rule check (Repeated + Non-trivial + Generalizable + Real-pitfall)\n- v4.10.6 — html skill: presentation / design / flowchart / architecture HTML deliverables. Ships 3 reference templates (tabbed_design, presentation_slides, flowchart_page). Screenshot-iteration loop for SageMaker (no Playwright).\n- v4.10.7 — destructive-command hardening: ~50 new bash DANGEROUS_PATTERNS + ~12 new python DANGEROUS_PYTHON patterns. HIGH_RISK_TOOLS = {bash, python_exec, task, web_fetch} excluded from Always-Approve UI. 107-case test coverage. Cross-surface mirrored into Claude Code + Learning_Factory hooks.\n- v4.10.8 — obfuscation hardening + recursive folder removal hard-block. Bash: base64-decode pipe to extended interpreter set, xxd/od/hexdump decode chains, recursive `rm`/`rmdir`/PowerShell `Remove-Item -Recurse`. Python: blanket `shutil.rmtree`/`os.rmdir`/`os.removedirs`/`Path.rmdir` block from `python_exec`. 129-case test coverage.\n- v4.10.9 — backtick eval+downloader parity. One narrow new pattern catching `eval` + backtick + remote-fetcher (`curl`/`wget`/`fetch`) or decoder (`base64`/`xxd`/`hexdump`). Defense-in-depth only — `eval` is already excluded from v4's bash allowlist, zero new false-positive risk. 134-case test coverage.\n- **v4.10.10** — `aws_bedrock_only` UI toggle. Cell 2 gains a \"Bedrock-only\" checkbox (default ticked = strict). Untick to allow S3 read/write, Textract, Lambda invoke, DynamoDB writes — all with approval; destructive AWS ops remain hard-blocked. Cell 3 banner displays current AWS scope. Inline `(?i)` flag on PowerShell `Remove-Item` regex (belt-and-suspenders — `re.IGNORECASE` is already applied at the matching layer; explicit flag survives future refactor). Codex comprehensive review: PASS. Real coding bugs found: 0.\n\n**Full docs:** See `USER_GUIDE.md` for complete documentation.\n"

Runs skills either inline (default) OR forked (executes the skill prompt in an isolated sub-agent with its own token budget via `runAgent` + `prepareForkedCommandContext`). compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-l-iter2.md:4773:compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2349:.\compact_v5\_phase_2\v4_reference\chat.ipynb:6:   "source": "# SageAgent V4.10.10\n\n**Setup:** Run cells 1-3 in order:\n- **Cell 1** installs packages (run once per kernel).\n- **Cell 2** shows config widgets â€” set Model, Temperature, Workspace, Mock-Mode, and the **Bedrock-only** checkbox (default ticked = strict; untick to allow S3 / Textract / Lambda / DynamoDB writes with approval).\n- **Cell 3** reads all widget values into `CONFIG` and launches the agent. The \"Configuration Applied\" banner displays the chosen AWS scope.\n\n**Core files:** `sagemaker_agent.py` (the entire agent) + this notebook + `memory.md` (auto-populated) + `AGENT_STATUS.md` (long-running handoff) + `skills/` (10 skills + `/reflexion`).\n\n**v4.9 highlights** (full notes in `changelogs/CHANGELOG_v4.9.X.md`):\n- v4.9.0 â€” `auto_trigger: false` honoured; word-boundary keyword match; SYSTEM_PROMPT critique-handling section\n- v4.9.1 â€” `/unskill <name>` + sticky deactivation\n- v4.9.2 â€” minimum-ship zip\n- v4.9.3 â€” prompt-injection scanner; CSO description validator; `/reflexion` skill\n- v4.9.4 â€” IterationBudget shared parent+sub-agents; ErrorClassifier + jittered backoff; pre-compact tool-result pruning; opt-in auxiliary-model compaction (Haiku); structured Resolved/Pending Questions in summary\n- v4.9.5 â€” opt-in self-patching skills (agent proposes SKILL.md improvements, you review via `/skill suggestions` then `/skill apply <name>`)\n- v4.9.6 â€” production hardening: no default skill auto-load, Bedrock-safe compact history, fixed build worktree isolation, dirty-state worktree overlay, serialized parallel builds, durable status doc, local-git-only SageMaker policy\n- v4.9.7 â€” `/context` diagnostic: context percentage, top tool-output sources, duplicate file reads, suggested action\n- v4.10.0 â€” Runnable parity (5 phases): notebook_edit (surgical .ipynb cell editor), skill listing token budget cap, per-sub-agent env-details, model-aware context window auto-derive, reactive compact on Bedrock CONTEXT_OVERFLOW. 5 Codex per-phase reviews, 9 correctness issues caught and fixed.\n- v4.10.1 â€” same-day follow-up: segment-level Context Collapse (collapses 3+ stale tool round-trips into one synthetic Bedrock-safe pair) + default model switched to Sonnet 4.5 (cache activates from 1024 tokens vs Haiku 4096).\n- v4.10.2 â€” verify-contract softened: now SUGGEST /verify after 3+ logic edits and wait for user confirm; strict mode opt-in via CONFIG.enforce_verify_contract=True (Codex caught the prompt contradiction)\n- v4.10.3 â€” production-readiness review apply: ship-gate verifier (verify_ship_zip.py), cache-boundary regression test (6 tests), many-skill stress test (100/1000 skills), clearer permission denials\n- v4.10.4 â€” sub-agent work-context handoff (bounded AGENT_STATUS slice + active todos + last 10 changed files), Codex follow-up review fix\n- v4.10.5 â€” Learning_Factory pattern adoption: post-compact resume protocol + structured summary sections (#12 Standing Constraints + #13 Critical Don't-Forget) + skill self-patching 4-rule check (Repeated + Non-trivial + Generalizable + Real-pitfall)\n- v4.10.6 â€” html skill: presentation / design / flowchart / architecture HTML deliverables. Ships 3 reference templates (tabbed_design, presentation_slides, flowchart_page). Screenshot-iteration loop for SageMaker (no Playwright).\n- v4.10.7 â€” destructive-command hardening: ~50 new bash DANGEROUS_PATTERNS + ~12 new python DANGEROUS_PYTHON patterns. HIGH_RISK_TOOLS = {bash, python_exec, task, web_fetch} excluded from Always-Approve UI. 107-case test coverage. Cross-surface mirrored into Claude Code + Learning_Factory hooks.\n- v4.10.8 â€” obfuscation hardening + recursive folder removal hard-block. Bash: base64-decode pipe to extended interpreter set, xxd/od/hexdump decode chains, recursive `rm`/`rmdir`/PowerShell `Remove-Item -Recurse`. Python: blanket `shutil.rmtree`/`os.rmdir`/`os.removedirs`/`Path.rmdir` block from `python_exec`. 129-case test coverage.\n- v4.10.9 â€” backtick eval+downloader parity. One narrow new pattern catching `eval` + backtick + remote-fetcher (`curl`/`wget`/`fetch`) or decoder (`base64`/`xxd`/`hexdump`). Defense-in-depth only â€” `eval` is already excluded from v4's bash allowlist, zero new false-positive risk. 134-case test coverage.\n- **v4.10.10** â€” `aws_bedrock_only` UI toggle. Cell 2 gains a \"Bedrock-only\" checkbox (default ticked = strict). Untick to allow S3 read/write, Textract, Lambda invoke, DynamoDB writes â€” all with approval; destructive AWS ops remain hard-blocked. Cell 3 banner displays current AWS scope. Inline `(?i)` flag on PowerShell `Remove-Item` regex (belt-and-suspenders â€” `re.IGNORECASE` is already applied at the matching layer; explicit flag survives future refactor). Codex comprehensive review: PASS. Real coding bugs found: 0.\n\n**Full docs:** See `USER_GUIDE.md` for complete documentation.\n"

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-i-iter2.md:2422:compact_v5/_status\codex_reviews\block-b-iter1.md:5292:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3592:.\_archive\compact_v3\ship\chat.ipynb:35:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Action | How |\n|--------|-----|\n| **Send message** | Type in input box, press Send |\n| **Stop agent** | Click Stop button |\n| **Check cost** | Type `/cost` |\n| **Code review** | Type `/review filename.py` |\n| **Explain code** | Type `/explain filename.py` |\n| **Generate tests** | Type `/test filename.py` |\n| **Verify project** | Type `/verify` |\n| **Apply standards** | Type `/standards filename.py` |\n| **Revert file** | Type `/revert filename.py` or `/revert all` |\n| **Compact context** | Click Compact button (or auto at 80%) |\n| **Clean traces** | Click Clean button (removes audit/snapshots, keeps sessions) |\n| **Save/Load** | Save button (auto-saves each message) / Session dropdown + Load |\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\n| Task | What to type |\n|------|-------------|\n| Read a file | \"Read app.py\" |\n| Find files | \"Find all Python files in this project\" |\n| Fix a bug | \"Read app.py, find the bug, and fix it\" |\n| Create chart | \"Create a bar chart from sales.csv showing revenue by product\" |\n| Create report | \"Create a Word report summarizing the data in results.csv\" |\n| Run command | \"Run git status\" |\n| Analyze image | \"Look at screenshot.png and describe what you see\" |\n| Search code | \"Find where authentication is handled in this codebase\" |\n\n## 22 Tools\n\n| Category | Tools | Approval? |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. Context auto-compacts at 80% usage (prune old tool outputs, then LLM summarize if needed)\n\n## Token Overhead Per API Call\n\n| Component | Tokens |\n|-----------|--------|\n| System prompt | ~1,200 |\n| Tool schemas | ~1,800 (lazy-load: ~1,200 for coding tasks) |\n| Bedrock overhead | ~346 |\n| **Total per call** | **~3,350** |\n\n## Session Management\n\n| Feature | How |\n|---------|-----|\n| **Auto-save** | Every message auto-saves (messages, todos, metadata) |\n| **Load session** | Session dropdown + Load button |\n| **New session** | New button (clears all state) |\n| **Checkpoints** | `/checkpoint name` (saves snapshot, max 50) |\n\n## Commands vs Skills\n\n| Method | How | Depth | Persists? |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. Commands cover the same categories with less detail.\n\n## Config\n\nDefault config is set in Cell 3 (before launch). Change model, temperature, thinking mode anytime in the chatbot UI during use.\n\nKey security settings (Cell 3):\n- `aws_bedrock_only = True` \u2014 blocks all AWS except Bedrock\n- `session_cost_limit = 1.0` \u2014 max $1 per session\n- `require_tool_approval = True` \u2014 approve/deny before execution"

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-i-iter2.md:2776:compact_v5/_status\codex_reviews\block-i-iter2.md:509:+| 083 | 2026-05-03 | Block I (Axis C closure) | Codex Block I iter-1 AXIS C — undeclared cross-references | _status/V5_RUNNABLE_PORT_LOG.md (this row) + ADR-029 §6 | doc-only | PASS | (no code change) | (pending) | Codex iter-1 AXIS C cleanup row. (a) **I-12 frontmatter parser improvements** (R8 #24, #50): DEFERRED to Block N per ADR-029 §6 (architectural fit — frontmatter expansion lands with Block N's dynamic-section + AGENTS.md infrastructure). (b) **Wave 6 row #93** (`PORT_LOG enumerates skills/verify/ as bundled`): closed via existing PORT_LOG #029 (Phase-10 byte-for-byte copy of 10 v4 production skills including verify). Block I makes no change to the bundled set; Phase-10 row is the canonical evidence. (c) **Wave 6 gap #8 — tool-vs-skill precedence** (PS_Plan_Edge_Cases_Thinking.md #93 / W6_multi_file_tasks.md:327-371): v5 disposition is **tools win for offline SageMaker / Bedrock-only deployments** because Block T's document tools (create_word, create_excel, create_chart, etc.) are zero-network-dependency and run inside the agent process; bundled skills (Runnable's debug, remember, etc.) are designed for the network-rich Anthropic-API-direct world and may reference tools that v5 doesn't ship (constraint #9 + #10). The model resolves a request by: (1) check direct tool registry first; (2) if no tool fits, check active skill body; (3) only suggest /skill use <name> when the user's task explicitly maps to a skill's CSO description. Block I lands the bundled debug + remember skills but they are auxiliary surfaces, not replacements for tools. ADR-029. | NEEDS-ADAPTATION per Wave 5-DEEP §Block F2: Runnable's tokenBudget tracks turn-output-tokens vs a user-set token budget parsed from the message text ("+500k"); v5 reuses the existing IterationBudget surface (counts turns) — same semantic, fewer surfaces, matches scenario #21 wording. DIMINISHING_THRESHOLD adapted from 500 tokens → 2 iterations. Cost-cap halt added (Wave 6 NLT row #21): even when iter_used < 90%, if session_cost ≥ session_cost_limit → halt. Sub-agents always halt (parent-only auto-continuation, matches Runnable agentId early-out at tokenBudget.ts:51). Default-OFF opt-in (Wave 6 NLT row #21 contract). Tracker reset to None at run() entry — never leaks state across user messages. F2 logic best-effort wrapped in try/except so it never blocks normal end_turn. Lock tests: 14 in test_block_f2.py — 7 pure-function (continue-under-90 / stop-at-90 / cost-cap / subagent / diminishing-after-3 / no-budget / message-format) + 3 TEST_DESIGN-named (auto_continue_at_under_90pct / blocks_at_90pct / respects_cost_cap) + 4 behavioral locks (default-off-no-continuation, diminishing-returns-end-to-end, subagent-no-auto-continue, tracker-resets-between-runs). ADR-028. |

(b) **Wave 6 row #93** (`PORT_LOG enumerates skills/verify/ as bundled`): closed via existing PORT_LOG #029 (Phase-10 byte-for-byte copy of 10 v4 production skills including verify). Block I makes no change to the bundled set; Phase-10 row is the canonical evidence. (c) **Wave 6 gap #8 — tool-vs-skill precedence** (PS_Plan_Edge_Cases_Thinking.md #93 / W6_multi_file_tasks.md:327-371): v5 disposition is **tools win for offline SageMaker / Bedrock-only deployments** because Block T's document tools (create_word, create_excel, create_chart, etc.) are zero-network-dependency and run inside the agent process; bundled skills (Runnable's debug, remember, etc.) are designed for the network-rich Anthropic-API-direct world and may reference tools that v5 doesn't ship (constraint #9 + #10). The model resolves a request by: (1) check direct tool registry first; (2) if no tool fits, check active skill body; (3) only suggest /skill use <name> when the user's task explicitly maps to a skill's CSO description. Block I lands the bundled debug + remember skills but they are auxiliary surfaces, not replacements for tools. ADR-029. | NEEDS-ADAPTATION per Wave 5-DEEP §Block F2: Runnable's tokenBudget tracks turn-output-tokens vs a user-set token budget parsed from the message text ("+500k"); v5 reuses the existing IterationBudget surface (counts turns) — same semantic, fewer surfaces, matches scenario #21 wording. DIMINISHING_THRESHOLD adapted from 500 tokens → 2 iterations. Cost-cap halt added (Wave 6 NLT row #21): even when iter_used < 90%, if session_cost ≥ session_cost_limit → halt. Sub-agents always halt (parent-only auto-continuation, matches Runnable agentId early-out at tokenBudget.ts:51). Default-OFF opt-in (Wave 6 NLT row #21 contract). Tracker reset to None at run() entry — never leaks state across user messages. F2 logic best-effort wrapped in try/except so it never blocks normal end_turn. Lock tests: 14 in test_block_f2.py — 7 pure-function (continue-under-90 / stop-at-90 / cost-cap / subagent / diminishing-after-3 / no-budget / message-format) + 3 TEST_DESIGN-named (auto_continue_at_under_90pct / blocks_at_90pct / respects_cost_cap) + 4 behavioral locks (default-off-no-continuation, diminishing-returns-end-to-end, subagent-no-auto-continue, tracker-resets-between-runs). ADR-028. |

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-i-iter2.md:3252:compact_v5/_status\codex_reviews\block-i-iter1.md:2765:compact_v5/_phase_2\synthesis\V5_PHASE_2_PLAN_v3.md:12:> **Wave 6 small deltas (2026-05-01)** — 111 user scenarios verified, 9 POSSIBLE-GAPs closed within existing Blocks: Block C+ +30 LOC ipywidgets fallback (60s watchdog + ask_user text mode); Block G +5 LOC `MAX_SUBAGENT_DEPTH=2`; Block E+F +10 LOC long-text `<details>` collapse; **Block H+ Auto-Dream is MANUAL-TRIGGER ONLY (user decision 2026-05-01)** — no daemon, no auto-fire; only runs when user invokes `/dream` slash command (Block D). USER_GUIDE must document `/dream` usage clearly: "Run `/dream` when memory.md or AGENT_STATUS.md feel cluttered after long sessions; it forks a sub-agent that consolidates+prunes+indexes your memory files. Costs ~$0.01-0.05 in API calls. Safe to run anytime, idempotent." Plus doc rows for mock_mode disclaimer + ipywidgets pin + PermissionDialog Q1 row + Block I tool-vs-skill precedence + create_html design note. Plan total: 21 Blocks, ~19,345 LOC (+0.23%); lock tests 95 → 135.

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-i-iter2.md:3432:compact_v5/_status\codex_reviews\block-i-iter2.md:509:+| 083 | 2026-05-03 | Block I (Axis C closure) | Codex Block I iter-1 AXIS C — undeclared cross-references | _status/V5_RUNNABLE_PORT_LOG.md (this row) + ADR-029 §6 | doc-only | PASS | (no code change) | (pending) | Codex iter-1 AXIS C cleanup row. (a) **I-12 frontmatter parser improvements** (R8 #24, #50): DEFERRED to Block N per ADR-029 §6 (architectural fit — frontmatter expansion lands with Block N's dynamic-section + AGENTS.md infrastructure). (b) **Wave 6 row #93** (`PORT_LOG enumerates skills/verify/ as bundled`): closed via existing PORT_LOG #029 (Phase-10 byte-for-byte copy of 10 v4 production skills including verify). Block I makes no change to the bundled set; Phase-10 row is the canonical evidence. (c) **Wave 6 gap #8 — tool-vs-skill precedence** (PS_Plan_Edge_Cases_Thinking.md #93 / W6_multi_file_tasks.md:327-371): v5 disposition is **tools win for offline SageMaker / Bedrock-only deployments** because Block T's document tools (create_word, create_excel, create_chart, etc.) are zero-network-dependency and run inside the agent process; bundled skills (Runnable's debug, remember, etc.) are designed for the network-rich Anthropic-API-direct world and may reference tools that v5 doesn't ship (constraint #9 + #10). The model resolves a request by: (1) check direct tool registry first; (2) if no tool fits, check active skill body; (3) only suggest /skill use <name> when the user's task explicitly maps to a skill's CSO description. Block I lands the bundled debug + remember skills but they are auxiliary surfaces, not replacements for tools. ADR-029. | NEEDS-ADAPTATION per Wave 5-DEEP §Block F2: Runnable's tokenBudget tracks turn-output-tokens vs a user-set token budget parsed from the message text ("+500k"); v5 reuses the existing IterationBudget surface (counts turns) — same semantic, fewer surfaces, matches scenario #21 wording. DIMINISHING_THRESHOLD adapted from 500 tokens → 2 iterations. Cost-cap halt added (Wave 6 NLT row #21): even when iter_used < 90%, if session_cost ≥ session_cost_limit → halt. Sub-agents always halt (parent-only auto-continuation, matches Runnable agentId early-out at tokenBudget.ts:51). Default-OFF opt-in (Wave 6 NLT row #21 contract). Tracker reset to None at run() entry — never leaks state across user messages. F2 logic best-effort wrapped in try/except so it never blocks normal end_turn. Lock tests: 14 in test_block_f2.py — 7 pure-function (continue-under-90 / stop-at-90 / cost-cap / subagent / diminishing-after-3 / no-budget / message-format) + 3 TEST_DESIGN-named (auto_continue_at_under_90pct / blocks_at_90pct / respects_cost_cap) + 4 behavioral locks (default-off-no-continuation, diminishing-returns-end-to-end, subagent-no-auto-continue, tracker-resets-between-runs). ADR-028. |

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-n-iter1.md:1472:compact_v5/_status/codex_reviews\block-g-iter2.md:1349: | 083 | 2026-05-03 | Block I (Axis C closure) | Codex Block I iter-1 AXIS C — undeclared cross-references | _status/V5_RUNNABLE_PORT_LOG.md (this row) + ADR-029 §6 | doc-only | PASS | (no code change) | 43d1ebe | Codex iter-1 AXIS C cleanup row. (a) **I-12 frontmatter parser improvements** (R8 #24, #50): DEFERRED to Block N per ADR-029 §6 (architectural fit — frontmatter expansion lands with Block N's dynamic-section + AGENTS.md infrastructure). (b) **Wave 6 row #93** (`PORT_LOG enumerates skills/verify/ as bundled`): closed via existing PORT_LOG #029 (Phase-10 byte-for-byte copy of 10 v4 production skills including verify). Block I makes no change to the bundled set; Phase-10 row is the canonical evidence. (c) **Wave 6 gap #8 — tool-vs-skill precedence** (PS_Plan_Edge_Cases_Thinking.md #93 / W6_multi_file_tasks.md:327-371): v5 disposition is **tools win for offline SageMaker / Bedrock-only deployments** because Block T's document tools (create_word, create_excel, create_chart, etc.) are zero-network-dependency and run inside the agent process; bundled skills (Runnable's debug, remember, etc.) are designed for the network-rich Anthropic-API-direct world and may reference tools that v5 doesn't ship (constraint #9 + #10). The model resolves a request by: (1) check direct tool registry first; (2) if no tool fits, check active skill body; (3) only suggest /skill use <name> when the user's task explicitly maps to a skill's CSO description. Block I lands the bundled debug + remember skills but they are auxiliary surfaces, not replacements for tools. ADR-029. |

Block I lands the bundled debug + remember skills but they are auxiliary surfaces, not replacements for tools. ADR-029. |

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-m-iter1.md:2187:compact_v5/_phase_2\v4_reference\chat.ipynb:6:   "source": "# SageAgent V4.10.10\n\n**Setup:** Run cells 1-3 in order:\n- **Cell 1** installs packages (run once per kernel).\n- **Cell 2** shows config widgets — set Model, Temperature, Workspace, Mock-Mode, and the **Bedrock-only** checkbox (default ticked = strict; untick to allow S3 / Textract / Lambda / DynamoDB writes with approval).\n- **Cell 3** reads all widget values into `CONFIG` and launches the agent. The \"Configuration Applied\" banner displays the chosen AWS scope.\n\n**Core files:** `sagemaker_agent.py` (the entire agent) + this notebook + `memory.md` (auto-populated) + `AGENT_STATUS.md` (long-running handoff) + `skills/` (10 skills + `/reflexion`).\n\n**v4.9 highlights** (full notes in `changelogs/CHANGELOG_v4.9.X.md`):\n- v4.9.0 — `auto_trigger: false` honoured; word-boundary keyword match; SYSTEM_PROMPT critique-handling section\n- v4.9.1 — `/unskill <name>` + sticky deactivation\n- v4.9.2 — minimum-ship zip\n- v4.9.3 — prompt-injection scanner; CSO description validator; `/reflexion` skill\n- v4.9.4 — IterationBudget shared parent+sub-agents; ErrorClassifier + jittered backoff; pre-compact tool-result pruning; opt-in auxiliary-model compaction (Haiku); structured Resolved/Pending Questions in summary\n- v4.9.5 — opt-in self-patching skills (agent proposes SKILL.md improvements, you review via `/skill suggestions` then `/skill apply <name>`)\n- v4.9.6 — production hardening: no default skill auto-load, Bedrock-safe compact history, fixed build worktree isolation, dirty-state worktree overlay, serialized parallel builds, durable status doc, local-git-only SageMaker policy\n- v4.9.7 — `/context` diagnostic: context percentage, top tool-output sources, duplicate file reads, suggested action\n- v4.10.0 — Runnable parity (5 phases): notebook_edit (surgical .ipynb cell editor), skill listing token budget cap, per-sub-agent env-details, model-aware context window auto-derive, reactive compact on Bedrock CONTEXT_OVERFLOW. 5 Codex per-phase reviews, 9 correctness issues caught and fixed.\n- v4.10.1 — same-day follow-up: segment-level Context Collapse (collapses 3+ stale tool round-trips into one synthetic Bedrock-safe pair) + default model switched to Sonnet 4.5 (cache activates from 1024 tokens vs Haiku 4096).\n- v4.10.2 — verify-contract softened: now SUGGEST /verify after 3+ logic edits and wait for user confirm; The \"Configuration Applied\" banner displays the chosen AWS scope.\n\n**Core files:** `sagemaker_agent.py` (the entire agent) + this notebook + `memory.md` (auto-populated) + `AGENT_STATUS.md` (long-running handoff) + `skills/` (10 skills + `/reflexion`).\n\n**v4.9 highlights** (full notes in `changelogs/CHANGELOG_v4.9.X.md`):\n- v4.9.0 â€” `auto_trigger: false` honoured; word-boundary keyword match; SYSTEM_PROMPT critique-handling section\n- v4.9.1 â€” `/unskill <name>` + sticky deactivation\n- v4.9.2 â€” minimum-ship zip\n- v4.9.3 â€” prompt-injection scanner; CSO description validator; `/reflexion` skill\n- v4.9.4 â€” IterationBudget shared parent+sub-agents; ErrorClassifier + jittered backoff; pre-compact tool-result pruning; opt-in auxiliary-model compaction (Haiku); structured Resolved/Pending Questions in summary\n- v4.9.5 â€” opt-in self-patching skills (agent proposes SKILL.md improvements, you review via `/skill suggestions` then `/skill apply <name>`)\n- v4.9.6 â€” production hardening: no default skill auto-load, Bedrock-safe compact history, fixed build worktree isolation, dirty-state worktree overlay, serialized parallel builds, durable status doc, local-git-only SageMaker policy\n- v4.9.7 â€” `/context` diagnostic: context percentage, top tool-output sources, duplicate file reads, suggested action\n- v4.10.0 â€” Runnable parity (5 phases): notebook_edit (surgical .ipynb cell editor), skill listing token budget cap, per-sub-agent env-details, model-aware context window auto-derive, reactive compact on Bedrock CONTEXT_OVERFLOW. 5 Codex per-phase reviews, 9 correctness issues caught and fixed.\n- v4.10.1 â€” same-day follow-up: segment-level Context Collapse (collapses 3+ stale tool round-trips into one synthetic Bedrock-safe pair) + default model switched to Sonnet 4.5 (cache activates from 1024 tokens vs Haiku 4096).\n- v4.10.2 â€” verify-contract softened: now SUGGEST /verify after 3+ logic edits and wait for user confirm; strict mode opt-in via CONFIG.enforce_verify_contract=True (Codex caught the prompt contradiction)\n- v4.10.3 â€” production-readiness review apply: ship-gate verifier (verify_ship_zip.py), cache-boundary regression test (6 tests), many-skill stress test (100/1000 skills), clearer permission denials\n- v4.10.4 â€” sub-agent work-context handoff (bounded AGENT_STATUS slice + active todos + last 10 changed files), Codex follow-up review fix\n- v4.10.5 â€” Learning_Factory pattern adoption: post-compact resume protocol + structured summary sections (#12 Standing Constraints + #13 Critical Don't-Forget) + skill self-patching 4-rule check (Repeated + Non-trivial + Generalizable + Real-pitfall)\n- v4.10.6 â€” html skill: presentation / design / flowchart / architecture HTML deliverables. Ships 3 reference templates (tabbed_design, presentation_slides, flowchart_page). Screenshot-iteration loop for SageMaker (no Playwright).\n- v4.10.7 â€” destructive-command hardening: ~50 new bash DANGEROUS_PATTERNS + ~12 new python DANGEROUS_PYTHON patterns. HIGH_RISK_TOOLS = {bash, python_exec, task, web_fetch} excluded from Always-Approve UI. 107-case test coverage. Cross-surface mirrored into Claude Code + Learning_Factory hooks.\n- v4.10.8 â€” obfuscation hardening + recursive folder removal hard-block. Bash: base64-decode pipe to extended interpreter set, xxd/od/hexdump decode chains, recursive `rm`/`rmdir`/PowerShell `Remove-Item -Recurse`. Python: blanket `shutil.rmtree`/`os.rmdir`/`os.removedirs`/`Path.rmdir` block from `python_exec`. 129-case test coverage.\n- v4.10.9 â€” backtick eval+downloader parity. One narrow new pattern catching `eval` + backtick + remote-fetcher (`curl`/`wget`/`fetch`) or decoder (`base64`/`xxd`/`hexdump`). Defense-in-depth only â€” `eval` is already excluded from v4's bash allowlist, zero new false-positive risk. 134-case test coverage.\n- **v4.10.10** â€” `aws_bedrock_only` UI toggle. Cell 2 gains a \"Bedrock-only\" checkbox (default ticked = strict). Untick to allow S3 read/write, Textract, Lambda invoke, DynamoDB writes â€” all with approval; destructive AWS ops remain hard-blocked. Cell 3 banner displays current AWS scope. Inline `(?i)` flag on PowerShell `Remove-Item` regex (belt-and-suspenders â€” `re.IGNORECASE` is already applied at the matching layer; explicit flag survives future refactor). Codex comprehensive review: PASS. Real coding bugs found: 0.\n\n**Full docs:** See `USER_GUIDE.md` for complete documentation.\n"

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-m-iter1.md:3371:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3825:.\_archive\compact\chat.ipynb:172:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\nTry these prompts to test the agent:\n\n| Task | Example Prompt |\n|------|----------------|\n| **Explore** | \"List files in this directory\" |\n| **Read** | \"Read the README.md file\" |\n| **Search** | \"Find all Python files with test in the name\" |\n| **Semantic Search** | \"Find where authentication is handled\" |\n| **Edit** | \"Add a comment to the top of file.py\" |\n| **Execute** | \"Run git status\" |\n| **Create Excel** | \"Create an Excel file with employee data\" |\n| **Create Word** | \"Write a project summary document\" |\n| **Create PDF** | \"Create a PDF report with table and chart summary\" |\n| **Create Notebook** | \"Create a notebook that loads and analyzes data\" |\n| **Plan** | \"Help me build a REST API with Flask\" |\n\n---\n\n## Capabilities\n\n**22 Tools:**\n- File: `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `glob`, `grep`, `list_dir`\n- Shell: `bash`\n- Python: `python_exec`\n- Documents: `create_word`, `create_excel`, `create_markdown`, `create_notebook`, `create_pdf`\n- Charts: `create_chart` (inline display)\n- Vision: `view_image`\n- Search: `semantic_search` (AI-powered code search)\n- Skills/MCP: `skill_list`, `skill_read`, `mcp_call`, `subagent_run`\n- Planning: `todo_write`, `todo_read`\n\n**Security:**\n- Workspace boundary enforcement\n- Secret detection (API keys, passwords, tokens)\n- Dangerous command blocking and restricted execution mode\n- Tool approval is configurable via UI `Require Approval` (default OFF in SageMaker)\n- Audit logging and session persistence"

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-m-iter1.md:3384:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4433:.\_archive\compact_v3\MAIN\agent\v3_architecture.html:410:    <div class="explain">The Compactor implements a two-stage strategy borrowed from OpenCode: first prune old tool outputs (cheap, no API call), then if still over threshold, generate an LLM summary (costs one API call). f'Error: {str(e)}')\n        status_label.value = '<b style=\"color:#f44336;\">Ã¢â€”Â Error</b>'\n\ndef on_clear(b):\n    \"\"\"Clear chat and start new session.\"\"\"\n    global current_session, Calls:0</span>'\n    status_label.value = '<b style=\"color:#4caf50;\">Ã¢â€”Â Ready</b>'\n    render_chat()\n\ndef on_save(b):\n    \"\"\"Save current session.\"\"\"\n    if current_session:\n        sessions.save(current_session)\n        add_message('system', f'Session saved: {current_session.id}')\n        update_session_list()\n    else:\n        add_message('system', 'No session to style=\"color:#4caf50;\">Ã¢â€”Â Ready (New)</b>'\n\ndef on_compact(b):\n    \"\"\"Manually compact context.\"\"\"\n    if not agent:\n        add_message('system', 'No conversation to compact.')\n compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v4.md:1744:compact_v5/_phase_2\v4_reference\chat.ipynb:6:   "source": "# SageAgent V4.10.10\n\n**Setup:** Run cells 1-3 in order:\n- **Cell 1** installs packages (run once per kernel).\n- **Cell 2** shows config widgets â€” set Model, Temperature, Workspace, Mock-Mode, and the **Bedrock-only** checkbox (default ticked = strict; untick to allow S3 / Textract / Lambda / DynamoDB writes with approval).\n- **Cell 3** reads all widget values into `CONFIG` and launches the agent. The \"Configuration Applied\" banner displays the chosen AWS scope.\n\n**Core files:** `sagemaker_agent.py` (the entire agent) + this notebook + `memory.md` (auto-populated) + `AGENT_STATUS.md` (long-running handoff) + `skills/` (10 skills + `/reflexion`).\n\n**v4.9 highlights** (full notes in `changelogs/CHANGELOG_v4.9.X.md`):\n- v4.9.0 â€” `auto_trigger: false` honoured; word-boundary keyword match; SYSTEM_PROMPT critique-handling section\n- v4.9.1 â€” `/unskill <name>` + sticky deactivation\n- v4.9.2 â€” minimum-ship zip\n- v4.9.3 â€” prompt-injection scanner; CSO description validator; `/reflexion` skill\n- v4.9.4 â€” IterationBudget shared parent+sub-agents; ErrorClassifier + jittered backoff; pre-compact tool-result pruning; opt-in auxiliary-model compaction (Haiku); structured Resolved/Pending Questions in summary\n- v4.9.5 â€” opt-in self-patching skills (agent proposes SKILL.md improvements, you review via `/skill suggestions` then `/skill apply <name>`)\n- v4.9.6 â€” production hardening: no default skill auto-load, Bedrock-safe compact history, fixed build worktree isolation, dirty-state worktree overlay, serialized parallel builds, durable status doc, local-git-only SageMaker policy\n- v4.9.7 â€” `/context` diagnostic: context percentage, top tool-output sources, duplicate file reads, suggested action\n- v4.10.0 â€” Runnable parity (5 phases): notebook_edit (surgical .ipynb cell editor), skill listing token budget cap, per-sub-agent env-details, model-aware context window auto-derive, reactive compact on Bedrock CONTEXT_OVERFLOW. 5 Codex per-phase reviews, 9 correctness issues caught and fixed.\n- v4.10.1 â€” same-day follow-up: segment-level Context Collapse (collapses 3+ stale tool round-trips into one synthetic Bedrock-safe pair) + default model switched to Sonnet 4.5 (cache activates from 1024 tokens vs Haiku 4096).\n- v4.10.2 â€” verify-contract softened: now SUGGEST /verify after 3+ logic edits and wait for user confirm; strict mode opt-in via CONFIG.enforce_verify_contract=True (Codex caught the prompt contradiction)\n- v4.10.3 â€” production-readiness review apply: ship-gate verifier (verify_ship_zip.py), cache-boundary regression test (6 tests), many-skill stress test (100/1000 skills), clearer permission denials\n- v4.10.4 â€” sub-agent work-context handoff (bounded AGENT_STATUS slice + active todos + last 10 changed files), Codex follow-up review fix\n- v4.10.5 â€” Learning_Factory pattern adoption: post-compact resume protocol + structured summary sections (#12 Standing Constraints + #13 Critical Don't-Forget) + skill self-patching 4-rule check (Repeated + Non-trivial + Generalizable + Real-pitfall)\n- v4.10.6 â€” html skill: presentation / design / flowchart / architecture HTML deliverables. Ships 3 reference templates (tabbed_design, presentation_slides, flowchart_page). Screenshot-iteration loop for SageMaker (no Playwright).\n- v4.10.7 â€” destructive-command hardening: ~50 new bash DANGEROUS_PATTERNS + ~12 new python DANGEROUS_PYTHON patterns. HIGH_RISK_TOOLS = {bash, python_exec, task, web_fetch} excluded from Always-Approve UI. 107-case test coverage. Cross-surface mirrored into Claude Code + Learning_Factory hooks.\n- v4.10.8 â€” obfuscation hardening + recursive folder removal hard-block. Bash: base64-decode pipe to extended interpreter set, xxd/od/hexdump decode chains, recursive `rm`/`rmdir`/PowerShell `Remove-Item -Recurse`. Python: blanket `shutil.rmtree`/`os.rmdir`/`os.removedirs`/`Path.rmdir` block from `python_exec`. 129-case test coverage.\n- v4.10.9 â€” backtick eval+downloader parity. One narrow new pattern catching `eval` + backtick + remote-fetcher (`curl`/`wget`/`fetch`) or decoder (`base64`/`xxd`/`hexdump`). Defense-in-depth only â€” `eval` is already excluded from v4's bash allowlist, zero new false-positive risk. 134-case test coverage.\n- **v4.10.10** â€” `aws_bedrock_only` UI toggle. Cell 2 gains a \"Bedrock-only\" checkbox (default ticked = strict). Untick to allow S3 read/write, Textract, Lambda invoke, DynamoDB writes â€” all with approval; destructive AWS ops remain hard-blocked. Cell 3 banner displays current AWS scope. Inline `(?i)` flag on PowerShell `Remove-Item` regex (belt-and-suspenders â€” `re.IGNORECASE` is already applied at the matching layer; explicit flag survives future refactor). Codex comprehensive review: PASS. Real coding bugs found: 0.\n\n**Full docs:** See `USER_GUIDE.md` for complete documentation.\n"

compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:955:.\compact_v4\MAIN\agent\v3_architecture.html:476:    <div class="explain">The Compactor implements a two-stage strategy borrowed from OpenCode: first prune old tool outputs (cheap, no API call), then if still over threshold, generate an LLM summary (costs one API call). Protected tools (todo, semantic_search) are never pruned. The File Cache uses LRU eviction with mtime validation to prevent stale reads.</div>

compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:2349:.\compact_v5\_phase_2\v4_reference\chat.ipynb:6:   "source": "# SageAgent V4.10.10\n\n**Setup:** Run cells 1-3 in order:\n- **Cell 1** installs packages (run once per kernel).\n- **Cell 2** shows config widgets â€” set Model, Temperature, Workspace, Mock-Mode, and the **Bedrock-only** checkbox (default ticked = strict; untick to allow S3 / Textract / Lambda / DynamoDB writes with approval).\n- **Cell 3** reads all widget values into `CONFIG` and launches the agent. The \"Configuration Applied\" banner displays the chosen AWS scope.\n\n**Core files:** `sagemaker_agent.py` (the entire agent) + this notebook + `memory.md` (auto-populated) + `AGENT_STATUS.md` (long-running handoff) + `skills/` (10 skills + `/reflexion`).\n\n**v4.9 highlights** (full notes in `changelogs/CHANGELOG_v4.9.X.md`):\n- v4.9.0 â€” `auto_trigger: false` honoured; word-boundary keyword match; SYSTEM_PROMPT critique-handling section\n- v4.9.1 â€” `/unskill <name>` + sticky deactivation\n- v4.9.2 â€” minimum-ship zip\n- v4.9.3 â€” prompt-injection scanner; CSO description validator; `/reflexion` skill\n- v4.9.4 â€” IterationBudget shared parent+sub-agents; ErrorClassifier + jittered backoff; pre-compact tool-result pruning; opt-in auxiliary-model compaction (Haiku); structured Resolved/Pending Questions in summary\n- v4.9.5 â€” opt-in self-patching skills (agent proposes SKILL.md improvements, you review via `/skill suggestions` then `/skill apply <name>`)\n- v4.9.6 â€” production hardening: no default skill auto-load, Bedrock-safe compact history, fixed build worktree isolation, dirty-state worktree overlay, serialized parallel builds, durable status doc, local-git-only SageMaker policy\n- v4.9.7 â€” `/context` diagnostic: context percentage, top tool-output sources, duplicate file reads, suggested action\n- v4.10.0 â€” Runnable parity (5 phases): notebook_edit (surgical .ipynb cell editor), skill listing token budget cap, per-sub-agent env-details, model-aware context window auto-derive, reactive compact on Bedrock CONTEXT_OVERFLOW. 5 Codex per-phase reviews, 9 correctness issues caught and fixed.\n- v4.10.1 â€” same-day follow-up: segment-level Context Collapse (collapses 3+ stale tool round-trips into one synthetic Bedrock-safe pair) + default model switched to Sonnet 4.5 (cache activates from 1024 tokens vs Haiku 4096).\n- v4.10.2 â€” verify-contract softened: now SUGGEST /verify after 3+ logic edits and wait for user confirm; strict mode opt-in via CONFIG.enforce_verify_contract=True (Codex caught the prompt contradiction)\n- v4.10.3 â€” production-readiness review apply: ship-gate verifier (verify_ship_zip.py), cache-boundary regression test (6 tests), many-skill stress test (100/1000 skills), clearer permission denials\n- v4.10.4 â€” sub-agent work-context handoff (bounded AGENT_STATUS slice + active todos + last 10 changed files), Codex follow-up review fix\n- v4.10.5 â€” Learning_Factory pattern adoption: post-compact resume protocol + structured summary sections (#12 Standing Constraints + #13 Critical Don't-Forget) + skill self-patching 4-rule check (Repeated + Non-trivial + Generalizable + Real-pitfall)\n- v4.10.6 â€” html skill: presentation / design / flowchart / architecture HTML deliverables. Ships 3 reference templates (tabbed_design, presentation_slides, flowchart_page). Screenshot-iteration loop for SageMaker (no Playwright).\n- v4.10.7 â€” destructive-command hardening: ~50 new bash DANGEROUS_PATTERNS + ~12 new python DANGEROUS_PYTHON patterns. HIGH_RISK_TOOLS = {bash, python_exec, task, web_fetch} excluded from Always-Approve UI. 107-case test coverage. Cross-surface mirrored into Claude Code + Learning_Factory hooks.\n- v4.10.8 â€” obfuscation hardening + recursive folder removal hard-block. Bash: base64-decode pipe to extended interpreter set, xxd/od/hexdump decode chains, recursive `rm`/`rmdir`/PowerShell `Remove-Item -Recurse`. Python: blanket `shutil.rmtree`/`os.rmdir`/`os.removedirs`/`Path.rmdir` block from `python_exec`. 129-case test coverage.\n- v4.10.9 â€” backtick eval+downloader parity. One narrow new pattern catching `eval` + backtick + remote-fetcher (`curl`/`wget`/`fetch`) or decoder (`base64`/`xxd`/`hexdump`). Defense-in-depth only â€” `eval` is already excluded from v4's bash allowlist, zero new false-positive risk. 134-case test coverage.\n- **v4.10.10** â€” `aws_bedrock_only` UI toggle. Cell 2 gains a \"Bedrock-only\" checkbox (default ticked = strict). Untick to allow S3 read/write, Textract, Lambda invoke, DynamoDB writes â€” all with approval; destructive AWS ops remain hard-blocked. Cell 3 banner displays current AWS scope. Inline `(?i)` flag on PowerShell `Remove-Item` regex (belt-and-suspenders â€” `re.IGNORECASE` is already applied at the matching layer; explicit flag survives future refactor). Codex comprehensive review: PASS. Real coding bugs found: 0.\n\n**Full docs:** See `USER_GUIDE.md` for complete documentation.\n"

compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3592:.\_archive\compact_v3\ship\chat.ipynb:35:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Action | How |\n|--------|-----|\n| **Send message** | Type in input box, press Send |\n| **Stop agent** | Click Stop button |\n| **Check cost** | Type `/cost` |\n| **Code review** | Type `/review filename.py` |\n| **Explain code** | Type `/explain filename.py` |\n| **Generate tests** | Type `/test filename.py` |\n| **Verify project** | Type `/verify` |\n| **Apply standards** | Type `/standards filename.py` |\n| **Revert file** | Type `/revert filename.py` or `/revert all` |\n| **Compact context** | Click Compact button (or auto at 80%) |\n| **Clean traces** | Click Clean button (removes audit/snapshots, keeps sessions) |\n| **Save/Load** | Save button (auto-saves each message) / Session dropdown + Load |\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\n| Task | What to type |\n|------|-------------|\n| Read a file | \"Read app.py\" |\n| Find files | \"Find all Python files in this project\" |\n| Fix a bug | \"Read app.py, find the bug, and fix it\" |\n| Create chart | \"Create a bar chart from sales.csv showing revenue by product\" |\n| Create report | \"Create a Word report summarizing the data in results.csv\" |\n| Run command | \"Run git status\" |\n| Analyze image | \"Look at screenshot.png and describe what you see\" |\n| Search code | \"Find where authentication is handled in this codebase\" |\n\n## 22 Tools\n\n| Category | Tools | Approval? |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. Context auto-compacts at 80% usage (prune old tool outputs, then LLM summarize if needed)\n\n## Token Overhead Per API Call\n\n| Component | Tokens |\n|-----------|--------|\n| System prompt | ~1,200 |\n| Tool schemas | ~1,800 (lazy-load: ~1,200 for coding tasks) |\n| Bedrock overhead | ~346 |\n| **Total per call** | **~3,350** |\n\n## Session Management\n\n| Feature | How |\n|---------|-----|\n| **Auto-save** | Every message auto-saves (messages, todos, metadata) |\n| **Load session** | Session dropdown + Load button |\n| **New session** | New button (clears all state) |\n| **Checkpoints** | `/checkpoint name` (saves snapshot, max 50) |\n\n## Commands vs Skills\n\n| Method | How | Depth | Persists? |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. Commands cover the same categories with less detail.\n\n## Config\n\nDefault config is set in Cell 3 (before launch). Change model, temperature, thinking mode anytime in the chatbot UI during use.\n\nKey security settings (Cell 3):\n- `aws_bedrock_only = True` \u2014 blocks all AWS except Bedrock\n- `session_cost_limit = 1.0` \u2014 max $1 per session\n- `require_tool_approval = True` \u2014 approve/deny before execution"
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3825:.\_archive\compact\chat.ipynb:172:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\nTry these prompts to test the agent:\n\n| Task | Example Prompt |\n|------|----------------|\n| **Explore** | \"List files in this directory\" |\n| **Read** | \"Read the README.md file\" |\n| **Search** | \"Find all Python files with test in the name\" |\n| **Semantic Search** | \"Find where authentication is handled\" |\n| **Edit** | \"Add a comment to the top of file.py\" |\n| **Execute** | \"Run git status\" |\n| **Create Excel** | \"Create an Excel file with employee data\" |\n| **Create Word** | \"Write a project summary document\" |\n| **Create PDF** | \"Create a PDF report with table and chart summary\" |\n| **Create Notebook** | \"Create a notebook that loads and analyzes data\" |\n| **Plan** | \"Help me build a REST API with Flask\" |\n\n---\n\n## Capabilities\n\n**22 Tools:**\n- File: `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `glob`, `grep`, `list_dir`\n- Shell: `bash`\n- Python: `python_exec`\n- Documents: `create_word`, `create_excel`, `create_markdown`, `create_notebook`, `create_pdf`\n- Charts: `create_chart` (inline display)\n- Vision: `view_image`\n- Search: `semantic_search` (AI-powered code search)\n- Skills/MCP: `skill_list`, `skill_read`, `mcp_call`, `subagent_run`\n- Planning: `todo_write`, `todo_read`\n\n**Security:**\n- Workspace boundary enforcement\n- Secret detection (API keys, passwords, tokens)\n- Dangerous command blocking and restricted execution mode\n- Tool approval is configurable via UI `Require Approval` (default OFF in SageMaker)\n- Audit logging and session persistence"

compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4067:.\_archive\complete\agent.ipynb:41:   "source": "# Global state\ncurrent_session = None\nagent = None\npending_approval = None\n\n# Plan Mode System Prompt (OpenCode-style)\nPLAN_MODE_PROMPT = \"\"\"You are in PLAN MODE. Your task is to EXPLORE and CREATE A PLAN, NOT execute.\n\n# Plan Mode Rules\n1. **READ-ONLY**: You can ONLY use these tools:\n   - read_file, glob, grep, list_dir (explore codebase)\n   - todo_write, todo_read (track what you're planning)\n\n2. **NO WRITES**: Do NOT use:\n   - write_file, edit_file, bash, python_exec, create_word, create_excel\n\n3. **OUTPUT**: Create a detailed plan in your response:\n   - What needs to be done (steps)\n   - Which files need to be modified\n   - What changes will be made\n   - Any risks or considerations\n\n4. **FORMAT**: End your response with a plan summary like:\n   ```\n   ## Implementation Plan\n   1. [Step 1]\n   2. [Step 2]\n   ...\n\n   ## Files to Modify\n   - file1.py: [changes]\n   - file2.py: [changes]\n\n   ## Ready to Execute?\n   Turn off Plan Mode and send \"execute plan\" to proceed.\n   ```\n\nRemember: EXPLORE and PLAN only. No modifications!\n\"\"\"\n\n# Simple Compactor class (inline for complete version)\nclass SimpleCompactor:\n    PRUNE_PROTECT_TOKENS = 40000\n    PRUNE_MIN_SAVINGS = 10000\n    \n    @classmethod\n    def estimate_tokens(cls, text):\n        return len(str(text)) // 4\n    \n    @classmethod\n    def create_summary_prompt(cls):\n        \"\"\"Create summary prompt using Claude Code's 9-section format.\"\"\"\n        return \"\"\"<analysis>\nFirst, analyze the conversation to identify: main goal, technical concepts, files touched, errors encountered, and current progress.\n</analysis>\n\nCreate a detailed summary following these EXACT sections:\n\n1. **Primary Request and Intent**: What did the user explicitly ask for? What is their underlying goal?\n\n2. **Key Technical Concepts**: Technologies, frameworks, libraries, patterns discussed or used.\n\n3. **Files and Code Sections**: For each important file:\n   - File path (absolute)\n   - WHY it's important\n   - What changes were made (if any)\n   - Key code snippets (if relevant)\n\n4. **Errors and Fixes**: For each error encountered:\n   - The error message\n   - How it was fixed\n   - Any user feedback on the fix\n\n5. **Problem Solving**: Problems solved during the session, and any ongoing issues still unresolved.\n\n6. **ALL User Messages**: List EVERY user message verbatim (this prevents intent drift):\n   - \"message 1 exact text\"\n   - \"message 2 exact text\"\n   - (continue for all messages)\n\n7. **Pending Tasks**: Tasks mentioned but not yet completed.\n\n8. **Current Work**: Precise current state including:\n   - What step we're on\n   - What was just completed\n   - Relevant code context\n\n9. **Next Step**: Only if directly in line with user's explicit request. Include direct quotes from user if applicable.\n\nFormat as a comprehensive summary that preserves all context needed to continue seamlessly.\"\"\"\n    \n    @classmethod\n    def prune_tool_outputs(cls, messages, max_tokens):\n        \"\"\"Prune old tool outputs, keep recent ones.\"\"\"\n        pruned = []\n        total_protected = 0\n        tokens_saved = 0\n        \n status_label.value = '<b style=\"color:#4caf50;\">â— Ready</b>'\n    render_chat()\n\ndef on_save(b):\n    \"\"\"Save current session.\"\"\"\n    if current_session:\n compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4101:.\_archive\compact_v2\REVIEW_AUDIT.md:111:- All core features working (MCP, sub-agents, skills, config, commands, cost, snapshots, permissions, diffs, web_fetch, ask_user)
compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4116:.\_archive\compact_v2\MAIN\agent\chat.ipynb:6:   "source": "# SageMaker Coding Agent V2\n\nSecure AI coding assistant powered by AWS Bedrock Claude.\n\n**22 Tools:** File ops, bash/python exec, docs/charts/pdf/notebooks, vision, semantic search, todos, web fetch, skills, sub-agents, ask user\n\n**New in V2:**\n- External config (`opencode.json`) with JSONC support\n- Skills system (`/skills`, `/skill use <name>`, `/skill clear`)\n- Custom slash commands with templates (`/review`, `/test`, etc.)\n- Sub-agents (build, plan, explore, general) via `task` tool\n- MCP client (local stdio + remote HTTP servers)\n- Cost tracking (`/cost`) with per-model Bedrock pricing\n- Snapshot & revert (`/revert <file>`, `/revert all`)\n- Interactive questions (`ask_user` tool)\n- Diff tracking on every edit\n- Permission rules (per-tool, file-pattern, command-pattern)\n- SSRF-hardened web fetch\n- Bedrock client config (600s read timeout for large outputs)\n- Python sandbox: C-extension accelerator whitelist + relative import support\n- SageMaker deadlock fix (Send button fallback for approval dialogs)\n\n**Security:** 3-layer bash + 3-layer Python + workspace boundary + SSRF protection\n\nSee `USER_GUIDE.md` for full documentation."
