compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:4429:.\_archive\compact_v3\MAIN\agent\chat.ipynb:35:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Action | How |\n|--------|-----|\n| **Send message** | Type in input box, press Send |\n| **Stop agent** | Click Stop button |\n| **Check cost** | Type `/cost` |\n| **Code review** | Type `/review filename.py` |\n| **Explain code** | Type `/explain filename.py` |\n| **Generate tests** | Type `/test filename.py` |\n| **Verify project** | Type `/verify` |\n| **Apply standards** | Type `/standards filename.py` |\n| **Revert file** | Type `/revert filename.py` or `/revert all` |\n| **Compact context** | Click Compact button (or auto at 80%) |\n| **Clean traces** | Click Clean button (removes audit/snapshots, keeps sessions) |\n| **Save/Load** | Save button (auto-saves each message) / Session dropdown + Load |\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\n| Task | What to type |\n|------|-------------|\n| Read a file | \"Read app.py\" |\n| Find files | \"Find all Python files in this project\" |\n| Fix a bug | \"Read app.py, find the bug, and fix it\" |\n| Create chart | \"Create a bar chart from sales.csv showing revenue by product\" |\n| Create report | \"Create a Word report summarizing the data in results.csv\" |\n| Run command | \"Run git status\" |\n| Analyze image | \"Look at screenshot.png and describe what you see\" |\n| Search code | \"Find where authentication is handled in this codebase\" |\n\n## 22 Tools\n\n| Category | Tools | Approval? |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. Context auto-compacts at 80% usage (prune old tool outputs, then LLM summarize if needed)\n\n## Token Overhead Per API Call\n\n| Component | Tokens |\n|-----------|--------|\n| System prompt | ~1,200 |\n| Tool schemas | ~1,800 (lazy-load: ~1,200 for coding tasks) |\n| Bedrock overhead | ~346 |\n| **Total per call** | **~3,350** |\n\n## Session Management\n\n| Feature | How |\n|---------|-----|\n| **Auto-save** | Every message auto-saves (messages, todos, metadata) |\n| **Load session** | Session dropdown + Load button |\n| **New session** | New button (clears all state) |\n| **Checkpoints** | `/checkpoint name` (saves snapshot, max 50) |\n\n## Commands vs Skills\n\n| Method | How | Depth | Persists? |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. Commands cover the same categories with less detail.\n\n## Config\n\nDefault config is set in Cell 3 (before launch). Change model, temperature, thinking mode anytime in the chatbot UI during use.\n\nKey security settings (Cell 3):\n- `aws_bedrock_only = True` \u2014 blocks all AWS except Bedrock\n- `session_cost_limit = 1.0` \u2014 max $1 per session\n- `require_tool_approval = True` \u2014 approve/deny before execution"

compact_v5\_phase_2\v4_reference\chat.ipynb:6:   "source": "# SageAgent V4.10.10\n\n**Setup:** Run cells 1-3 in order:\n- **Cell 1** installs packages (run once per kernel).\n- **Cell 2** shows config widgets — set Model, Temperature, Workspace, Mock-Mode, and the **Bedrock-only** checkbox (default ticked = strict; untick to allow S3 / Textract / Lambda / DynamoDB writes with approval).\n- **Cell 3** reads all widget values into `CONFIG` and launches the agent. The \"Configuration Applied\" banner displays the chosen AWS scope.\n\n**Core files:** `sagemaker_agent.py` (the entire agent) + this notebook + `memory.md` (auto-populated) + `AGENT_STATUS.md` (long-running handoff) + `skills/` (10 skills + `/reflexion`).\n\n**v4.9 highlights** (full notes in `changelogs/CHANGELOG_v4.9.X.md`):\n- v4.9.0 — `auto_trigger: false` honoured; word-boundary keyword match; SYSTEM_PROMPT critique-handling section\n- v4.9.1 — `/unskill <name>` + sticky deactivation\n- v4.9.2 — minimum-ship zip\n- v4.9.3 — prompt-injection scanner; CSO description validator; `/reflexion` skill\n- v4.9.4 — IterationBudget shared parent+sub-agents; ErrorClassifier + jittered backoff; pre-compact tool-result pruning; opt-in auxiliary-model compaction (Haiku); structured Resolved/Pending Questions in summary\n- v4.9.5 — opt-in self-patching skills (agent proposes SKILL.md improvements, you review via `/skill suggestions` then `/skill apply <name>`)\n- v4.9.6 — production hardening: no default skill auto-load, Bedrock-safe compact history, fixed build worktree isolation, dirty-state worktree overlay, serialized parallel builds, durable status doc, local-git-only SageMaker policy\n- v4.9.7 — `/context` diagnostic: context percentage, top tool-output sources, duplicate file reads, suggested action\n- v4.10.0 — Runnable parity (5 phases): notebook_edit (surgical .ipynb cell editor), skill listing token budget cap, per-sub-agent env-details, model-aware context window auto-derive, reactive compact on Bedrock CONTEXT_OVERFLOW. 5 Codex per-phase reviews, 9 correctness issues caught and fixed.\n- v4.10.1 — same-day follow-up: segment-level Context Collapse (collapses 3+ stale tool round-trips into one synthetic Bedrock-safe pair) + default model switched to Sonnet 4.5 (cache activates from 1024 tokens vs Haiku 4096).\n- v4.10.2 — verify-contract softened: now SUGGEST /verify after 3+ logic edits and wait for user confirm; strict mode opt-in via CONFIG.enforce_verify_contract=True (Codex caught the prompt contradiction)\n- v4.10.3 — production-readiness review apply: ship-gate verifier (verify_ship_zip.py), cache-boundary regression test (6 tests), many-skill stress test (100/1000 skills), clearer permission denials\n- v4.10.4 — sub-agent work-context handoff (bounded AGENT_STATUS slice + active todos + last 10 changed files), Codex follow-up review fix\n- v4.10.5 — Learning_Factory pattern adoption: post-compact resume protocol + structured summary sections (#12 Standing Constraints + #13 Critical Don't-Forget) + skill self-patching 4-rule check (Repeated + Non-trivial + Generalizable + Real-pitfall)\n- v4.10.6 — html skill: presentation / design / flowchart / architecture HTML deliverables. Ships 3 reference templates (tabbed_design, presentation_slides, flowchart_page). Screenshot-iteration loop for SageMaker (no Playwright).\n- v4.10.7 — destructive-command hardening: ~50 new bash DANGEROUS_PATTERNS + ~12 new python DANGEROUS_PYTHON patterns. HIGH_RISK_TOOLS = {bash, python_exec, task, web_fetch} excluded from Always-Approve UI. 107-case test coverage. Cross-surface mirrored into Claude Code + Learning_Factory hooks.\n- v4.10.8 — obfuscation hardening + recursive folder removal hard-block. Bash: base64-decode pipe to extended interpreter set, xxd/od/hexdump decode chains, recursive `rm`/`rmdir`/PowerShell `Remove-Item -Recurse`. Python: blanket `shutil.rmtree`/`os.rmdir`/`os.removedirs`/`Path.rmdir` block from `python_exec`. 129-case test coverage.\n- v4.10.9 — backtick eval+downloader parity. One narrow new pattern catching `eval` + backtick + remote-fetcher (`curl`/`wget`/`fetch`) or decoder (`base64`/`xxd`/`hexdump`). Defense-in-depth only — `eval` is already excluded from v4's bash allowlist, zero new false-positive risk. 134-case test coverage.\n- **v4.10.10** — `aws_bedrock_only` UI toggle. Cell 2 gains a \"Bedrock-only\" checkbox (default ticked = strict). Untick to allow S3 read/write, Textract, Lambda invoke, DynamoDB writes — all with approval; destructive AWS ops remain hard-blocked. Cell 3 banner displays current AWS scope. Inline `(?i)` flag on PowerShell `Remove-Item` regex (belt-and-suspenders — `re.IGNORECASE` is already applied at the matching layer; explicit flag survives future refactor). Codex comprehensive review: PASS. Real coding bugs found: 0.\n\n**Full docs:** See `USER_GUIDE.md` for complete documentation.\n"

compact_v5\_phase_2\v4_reference\USER_GUIDE.md:544:**Note on long-running status (v4.9.6):** `AGENT_STATUS.md` is loaded on every top-level run when `CONFIG.enable_status_doc = True` (default). compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:268:                <div class="card-desc">~50 new bash <code>DANGEROUS_PATTERNS</code> covering cloud destructive subcommands (AWS/GCP/Azure/PaaS/IaC/orchestration), git destructive (remote-branch del, <code>branch -D</code>, <code>tag -d</code>, <code>reflog expire</code>, <code>restore .</code>), storage tools (<code>lvremove</code>, <code>mkfs</code>, <code>dd of=/dev/</code>, <code>zfs destroy</code>, <code>cryptsetup luksClose</code>), persistence (<code>crontab -r</code>, <code>systemctl disable/stop</code>, <code>pm2 delete</code>), DB CLI inline (<code>DROP/TRUNCATE/DELETE FROM/FLUSHALL/SHUTDOWN</code>), system-path overwrite, perm lockout, <code>curl|sh</code>. ~12 new <code>DANGEROUS_PYTHON</code> patterns (<code>cursor.execute DROP</code>, SQLAlchemy <code>drop_all</code>, Mongo <code>dropDatabase/deleteMany</code>, Redis <code>flushall</code>, <code>os.unlink</code>/<code>shutil.rmtree</code> on system paths). <strong>HIGH_RISK_TOOLS = {bash, python_exec, task, web_fetch}</strong> excluded from Always-Approve UI shortcut — even with auto-approve on, these still prompt; the "Always Approve" button is hidden for them, so there's no UI path to a permanent bypass. Cross-surface: same denylist mirrored into <code>~/.claude/hooks/pre-bash-safety.sh</code> + Learning_Factory source-of-truth.</div>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:476:    <div class="explain">The Compactor implements a two-stage strategy borrowed from OpenCode: first prune old tool outputs (cheap, no API call), then if still over threshold, generate an LLM summary (costs one API call). Protected tools (todo, semantic_search) are never pruned. The File Cache uses LRU eviction with mtime validation to prevent stale reads.</div>

compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1137:        <strong>semantic_search</strong> &mdash; Searches your codebase by <em>meaning</em>, not just keywords. If you search "authentication logic", it finds code related to login/auth even if those exact words aren't used. Uses AWS Titan embeddings to convert code into vectors, then finds the most similar chunks. Python files are split by function/class (AST-aware), so results are more meaningful than line-based search.<br><br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1138:        <strong>web_fetch</strong> &mdash; Fetches a URL and converts the HTML to readable text. Protected against SSRF attacks: blocks requests to private IPs (10.x, 192.168.x, 127.0.0.1), blocks redirects to internal servers, limits response to 2MB. Useful for reading documentation or API specs from the web.
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1140:    <div class="explain"><strong>semantic_search</strong> uses Titan Embed v2 to vectorize code chunks, then cosine similarity to find matches by meaning rather than exact text. Requires an explicit <code>action="index"</code> call first (costs ~$0.01). In practice, <code>grep</code> handles 95% of search needs &mdash; semantic search is for cases where keyword matching fails. <strong>view_image</strong> base64-encodes the image and injects it as a content block into the next Claude API call for multimodal analysis.</div>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1155:        <strong>ask_user</strong> &mdash; Pauses the agent and asks you a question. Shows a text input with Submit/Skip buttons. The agent waits up to 5 minutes for your response, then continues based on your answer. Used when the agent needs clarification before proceeding.
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1157:    <div class="explain"><strong>Skills</strong> are injected into the system prompt at runtime, extending the agent's behavior without code changes. <strong>Sub-agents</strong> run as child sessions with scoped tool access and independent context, enabling parallel delegation. <strong>ask_user</strong> implements a blocking prompt with a 5-minute timeout, using threading.Event for synchronization between the agent thread and the UI thread.</div>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1164:        <strong>todo_write</strong> &mdash; Creates or updates a task list. Each task has a name, status (pending/in_progress/completed), and an active description. The agent uses this to plan multi-step work and track progress. The todo list persists with the session, so it survives across messages.<br><br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1165:        <strong>todo_read</strong> &mdash; Reads the current task list to check what's been done and what's remaining. The agent uses this to maintain awareness of its progress on complex tasks.<br><br>

   5: 6 v4 document tools consolidated (one file, minimum-file constraint #5):
   6: - create_word     â€” .docx via python-docx (lazy import).

   8: - create_markdown â€” .md trivial write.

  10: - create_chart    â€” .png via matplotlib (lazy import; supports chart_type).
  11: - create_pdf      â€” .pdf via matplotlib pdf backend (lazy import; supports
  12:                     heading/text/table/image content blocks).
  13: 
  14: Each tool fails fast with a clear error if its underlying library is
  15: missing. v5 doesn't pull these as hard dependencies (constraint #15) â€”
  16: SageMaker users with the standard Python data-science kernel have all
  17: of them installed.
  18: 
  19: Block T design note (test_tool_create_html_via_write_file_documented):
  20: There is intentionally NO `create_html` tool. Use `write_file` with a
  21: `.html` extension instead. HTML is text and `write_file` already works
  22: for it; adding a separate tool is bloat.
  23: """

  27: import os
  28: from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
  29:

  31:

  33: # ============================================================
  34: # create_word â€” python-docx
  35: # ============================================================
  36: 
  37: def _create_word_executor(args: Dict[str, Any], context: Optional[Dict] = None) -> str:
  38:     filepath = str(args.get("filepath") or args.get("file_path") or "").strip()
  39:     content = str(args.get("content") or "").strip()
  40:     if not filepath:
  41:         return "Error: filepath is required"
  42:     if not filepath.endswith(".docx"):
  43:         filepath += ".docx"
  44:     try:
  45:         from docx import Document
  46:     except ImportError:
  47:         return "Error: python-docx not installed; install via `pip install python-docx`"
  48:     try:
  49:         doc = Document()
  50:         # Treat lines starting with `# ` as H1, `## ` as H2, etc.
  51:         for line in content.splitlines():
  52:             stripped = line.strip()
  53:             if stripped.startswith("# "):
  54:                 doc.add_heading(stripped[2:], level=1)
  55:             elif stripped.startswith("## "):
  56:                 doc.add_heading(stripped[3:], level=2)
  57:             elif stripped.startswith("### "):
  58:                 doc.add_heading(stripped[4:], level=3)
  59:             elif stripped:
  60:                 doc.add_paragraph(stripped)
  61:             else:
  62:                 doc.add_paragraph("")
  63:         os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(filepath) or ".", exist_ok=True)
  64:         doc.save(filepath)
  65:         return f"Wrote {filepath}"
  66:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
  67:         return f"Error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
  68:

  31: def _build_index(path: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
  32:     """Build a TF-IDF index over text files under `path`."""
  33:     try:
  34:         from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
  35:     except ImportError:
  36:         raise RuntimeError("sklearn not installed; install via `pip install scikit-learn`")
  37: 
  38:     files: List[str] = []
  39:     docs: List[str] = []
  40:     p = Path(path)
  41:     if not p.is_dir() and not p.is_file():
  42:         return {"files": [], "docs": [], "vectorizer": None, "matrix": None}
  43:     if p.is_file():
  44:         try:
  45:             text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
  46:             files.append(str(p))
  47:             docs.append(text)
  48:         except OSError:
  49:             pass
  50:     else:
  51:         for fp in p.rglob("*"):
  52:             if not fp.is_file():
  53:                 continue
  54:             if fp.suffix.lower() not in (".py", ".md", ".txt", ".rst", ".html"):
  55:                 continue
  56:             try:
  57:                 text = fp.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
  58:                 files.append(str(fp))
  59:                 docs.append(text)
  60:             except OSError:
  61:                 continue
  62: 
  63:     if not docs:
  64:         return {"files": [], "docs": [], "vectorizer": None, "matrix": None}
  65: 
  66:     vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(stop_words="english", max_features=5000)
  67:     matrix = vectorizer.fit_transform(docs)
  68:     return {"files": files, "docs": docs, "vectorizer": vectorizer, "matrix": matrix}

  71: def _semantic_search_executor(args: Dict[str, Any], context: Optional[Dict] = None) -> str:
  72:     action = (args.get("action") or "search").lower()
  73:     path = args.get("path") or "."

  75:     if action == "index":

  77:             idx = _build_index(path)
  78:         except RuntimeError as exc:
  79:             return f"Error: {exc}"
  80:         _INDEX_CACHE[str(path)] = idx
  81:         return f"Indexed {len(idx['files'])} files from {path}."
  82: 
  83:     if action == "search":
  84:         query = str(args.get("query") or "").strip()
  85:         if not query:
  86:             return "Error: query is required for search action"

  89:         idx = _INDEX_CACHE.get(str(path))

  92:             idx = list(_INDEX_CACHE.values())[-1]

  21:     Not a full html2text replacement; v4 used html2text. v5 inlines a
  22:     minimal version to avoid the hard dep. Headings stay as # / ## /
  23:     ### markers; code blocks stay as triple-backtick; everything else
  24:     flattens to plain text.
  25:     """
  26:     text = html
  27:     # Headings.
  28:     for level in range(1, 4):
  29:         pattern = re.compile(rf"<h{level}[^>]*>(.*?)</h{level}>", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
  30:         text = pattern.sub(lambda m: "\n" + ("#" * level) + " " + re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", m.group(1)).strip() + "\n", text)
  31:     # Code blocks.
  32:     text = re.sub(r"<pre[^>]*>(.*?)</pre>", lambda m: "\n```\n" + re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", m.group(1)) + "\n```\n", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
  33:     # Paragraphs.
  34:     text = re.sub(r"<br\s*/?>", "\n", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
  35:     text = re.sub(r"</p>", "\n\n", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
  36:     # Strip remaining tags.
  37:     text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", text)
  38:     # Decode common entities.
  39:     text = (
  40:         text.replace("&amp;", "&")
  41:         .replace("&lt;", "<")
  42:         .replace("&gt;", ">")
  43:         .replace("&quot;", '"')
  44:         .replace("&#39;", "'")
  45:         .replace("&nbsp;", " ")
  46:     )
  47:     # Collapse whitespace.
  48:     text = re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", text)
  49:     text = re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", text)
  50:     return text.strip()
  51: 
  52: 
  53: def _web_fetch_executor(args: Dict[str, Any], context: Optional[Dict] = None) -> str:
  54:     url = str(args.get("url") or "").strip()
  55:     if not url:
  56:         return "Error: url is required"
  57:     if not (url.startswith("http://") or url.startswith("https://")):
  58:         return "Error: url must start with http:// or https://"
  59:     timeout = int(args.get("timeout_s") or 15)
  60:     try:
  61:         import requests
  62:     except ImportError:
  63:         return "Error: requests not installed; install via `pip install requests`"
  64:     try:
  65:         resp = requests.get(url, timeout=timeout)
  66:         resp.raise_for_status()
  67:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
  68:         return f"Error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
  69:     content_type = resp.headers.get("Content-Type", "").lower()
  70:     body = resp.text or ""
  71:     if "html" in content_type or body.lstrip().startswith(("<!doctype", "<html")):
  72:         return _html_to_markdown_lite(body)
  73:     return body
  74: 
  75: 
  76: _SCHEMA = {
  77:     "type": "object",
  78:     "properties": {
  79:         "url": {"type": "string"},
  80:         "timeout_s": {"type": "integer", "default": 15},
  81:     },
  82:     "required": ["url"],
  83: }
  84: 
  85: 
  86: def _register():
  87:     from .registry import find_tool_by_name, all_registered
  88:     if find_tool_by_name(all_registered(), "web_fetch") is not None:
  89:         return
  90:     register(build_tool(
  91:         name="web_fetch",
  92:         description="Fetch a URL and return its content as plain text / markdown.",
  93:         input_schema=_SCHEMA,
  94:         execute=_web_fetch_executor,
  95:         requires_approval=False,
  96:         should_defer=True,
  97:         max_result_size_chars=50000,
  98:     ))

  90: @dataclass
  91: class ToolRecord:

  93:     `BuiltTool<D>` returned by `buildTool(def)`. Defaults match Runnable's
  94:     `TOOL_DEFAULTS` (fail-closed: assume not concurrency-safe, assume

  98:     input_schema: Dict[str, Any]
  99:     execute: Callable[..., Any]

 101:     aliases: Tuple[str, ...] = ()
 102:     search_hint: str = ""
 103:     should_defer: bool = False
 104:     always_load: bool = False
 105: 
 106:     # Defaults are fail-closed for safety, mirroring Runnable's TOOL_DEFAULTS:
 107:     # - isConcurrencySafe â†’ false (assume not safe)
 108:     # - isReadOnly        â†’ false (assume writes)
 109:     # - isDestructive     â†’ false
 110:     # - isEnabled         â†’ true
 111:     is_read_only: bool = False
 112:     is_destructive: bool = False
 113:     is_concurrency_safe: bool = False
 114:     requires_approval: bool = False  # v4 split: defaults False, mutating tools set True
 115:     enabled: bool = True
 116:     max_result_size_chars: int = 50_000  # matches v4 max_output_chars + Runnable DEFAULT_MAX_RESULT_SIZE_CHARS
 117:

 119: def build_tool(
 120:     name: str,
 121:     description : str,  # spaced colon: see ToolDef Protocol comment above re: CSO hook regex.
 122:     input_schema: Dict[str, Any],
 123:     execute: Callable[..., Any],
 124:     **overrides: Any,
 125: ) -> ToolRecord:
 126:     """Construct a `ToolRecord` filling in safe defaults for omitted fields.
 127: 
 128:     Mirrors Runnable's `buildTool(def)` (`Tool.ts:783`). Tool authors only
 129:     have to specify what differs from defaults â€” most read-only tools just
 130:     need `is_read_only=True`; most mutating tools need `requires_approval=True`.
 131:     """
 132:     return ToolRecord(
 133:         name=name,
 134:         description=description,
 135:         input_schema=input_schema,
 136:         execute=execute,
 137:         **overrides,
 138:     )
 139: 
 140: 
 141: # ============================================================
 142: # Process-global registry
 143: # ============================================================
 144: 
 145: _REGISTRY: List[ToolRecord] = []
 146: 
 147: 
 148: def register(tool: ToolRecord) -> ToolRecord:
 149:     """Add a tool to the process-global registry. Returns the tool so
 150:     that module-level usage like `MY_TOOL = register(build_tool(...))`
 151:     is one expression."""
 152:     # Defensive: forbid duplicate names â€” silent overrides masked bugs in v4
 153:     # when two skills both registered "verify". Caller must explicitly
 154:     # `unregister(name)` first if they intend to replace.
 155:     for existing in _REGISTRY:
 156:         if existing.name == tool.name:
 157:             raise ValueError(
 158:                 f"Tool '{tool.name}' already registered. "
 159:                 f"Call unregister('{tool.name}') first if replacement is intended."
 160:             )
 161:     _REGISTRY.append(tool)
 162:     return tool
 163: 
 164: 
 165: def unregister(name: str) -> bool:
 166:     """Remove a tool by name. Returns True if a tool was removed."""
 167:     for i, tool in enumerate(_REGISTRY):
 168:         if tool.name == name:
 169:             del _REGISTRY[i]
 170:             return True
 171:     return False
 172: 
 173: 
 174: def all_registered() -> List[ToolRecord]:
 175:     """Return a snapshot copy of the current registry. Useful for tests."""
 176:     return list(_REGISTRY)
 177: 
 178: 
 179: # ============================================================
 180: # Lookup helpers (Runnable parity: toolMatchesName / findToolByName)
 181: # ============================================================
 182: 
 183: def tool_matches_name(tool: ToolRecord, name: str) -> bool:
 184:     """Runnable parity: `Tool.ts:toolMatchesName`."""
 185:     return tool.name == name or name in tool.aliases
 186: 
 187: 
 188: def find_tool_by_name(tools: Iterable[ToolRecord], name: str) -> Optional[ToolRecord]:
 189:     """Runnable parity: `Tool.ts:findToolByName`."""
 190:     for t in tools:
 191:         if tool_matches_name(t, name):
 192:             return t
 193:     return None
 194: 
 195: 
 196: # ============================================================
 197: # Public selection: get_tools + assemble_tool_pool
 198: # ============================================================
 199: 
 200: def _filter_by_deny_rules(
 201:     tools: Iterable[ToolRecord],
 202:     deny_rules: Optional[Set[str]],
 203: ) -> List[ToolRecord]:
 204:     """Runnable parity: `tools.ts:filterToolsByDenyRules` â†’
 205:     `permissions.ts:getDenyRuleForTool`. A tool is denied if any of these match:
 206:       - exact name match
 207:       - exact alias match
 208:       - MCP server-level prefix: a tool named `mcp__server__toolName` is
 209:         denied if the rule equals `mcp__server` (server blanket-deny)
 210:       - MCP server wildcard: rule `mcp__server__*` denies every tool with that
 211:         server prefix (Runnable supports both forms; we mirror both)
 212:     Non-MCP tool names ignore the MCP rules; MCP tool names also honor exact-
 213:     name and exact-alias rules. This matches Runnable's semantics where the
 214:     same matcher is reused at request time and at deny-filter time, so a
 215:     server-prefix rule strips ALL of that server's tools from the model's
 216:     view before the prompt is built."""
 217:     if not deny_rules:
 218:         return list(tools)
 219:     return [t for t in tools if not _is_denied(t, deny_rules)]
 220: 
 221: 
 222: def _is_denied(tool: ToolRecord, deny_rules: Set[str]) -> bool:
 223:     if tool.name in deny_rules:
 224:         return True
 225:     if any(a in deny_rules for a in tool.aliases):
 226:         return True
 227:     # MCP server-prefix match: a tool named `mcp__server__name` is denied by
 228:     # `mcp__server` (blanket-deny that whole server) or `mcp__server__*`
 229:     # (wildcard form). The first segment after `mcp__` is the server.
 230:     if tool.name.startswith("mcp__"):
 231:         parts = tool.name.split("__")
 232:         # parts = ["mcp", "<server>", "<toolName>"]; need at least 3 to have a server.
 233:         if len(parts) >= 3:
 234:             server = parts[1]
 235:             server_prefix = f"mcp__{server}"
 236:             if server_prefix in deny_rules or f"{server_prefix}__*" in deny_rules:
 237:                 return True
 238:     return False

 5909: def _normalise_ipynb_source(source) -> List[str]:
 5910:     """Convert source string to ipynb's list-of-lines format (with newlines)."""
 5911:     if isinstance(source, list):
 5912:         return source
 5913:     s = source if isinstance(source, str) else str(source or "")
 5914:     if not s:
 5915:         return [""]
 5916:     lines = s.split("\n")
 5917:     # ipynb format: every line ends with "\n" except the last
 5918:     return [ln + "\n" for ln in lines[:-1]] + [lines[-1]]

 5921: def tool_notebook_edit(args: Dict) -> str:
 5922:     """V4.10.0 #10: Edit a single cell in an existing .ipynb file.
 5923: 
 5924:     Args:
 5925:         path:        absolute or workspace-relative .ipynb file
 5926:         action:      "insert" | "replace" | "delete"
 5927:         cell_index:  0-based; -1 = append (insert only)
 5928:         cell_type:   "code" | "markdown" (required for insert/replace)
 5929:         source:      cell content (required for insert/replace)
 5930: 
 5931:     Returns:
 5932:         Status string with new cell count, or "Error: ..." on failure.
 5933:         Atomic: writes via tmp file + rename so a partial failure cannot
 5934:         corrupt the live notebook.
 5935:     """
 5936:     filepath = args.get("path") or args.get("filepath")
 5937:     action = (args.get("action") or "").lower()
 5938:     cell_index = args.get("cell_index", None)
 5939:     cell_type = (args.get("cell_type") or "").lower() or None
 5940:     source = args.get("source", None)
 5941: 
 5942:     if not filepath:
 5943:         return "Error: 'path' is required"
 5944:     if action not in _NOTEBOOK_EDIT_ACTIONS:
 5945:         return f"Error: 'action' must be one of {_NOTEBOOK_EDIT_ACTIONS}, got: {action!r}"
 5946:     if cell_index is None or not isinstance(cell_index, int):
 5947:         return "Error: 'cell_index' must be an integer (use -1 to append on insert)"
 5948:     if action in ("insert", "replace"):
 5949:         if cell_type not in _NOTEBOOK_CELL_TYPES:
 5950:             return f"Error: 'cell_type' must be one of {_NOTEBOOK_CELL_TYPES} for insert/replace"
 5951:         if source is None:
 5952:             return "Error: 'source' is required for insert/replace"
 5953: 
 5954:     if not os.path.isabs(filepath):
 5955:         filepath = os.path.join(CONFIG.workspace, filepath)
 5956:     if not filepath.endswith(".ipynb"):
 5957:         return f"Error: target must be a .ipynb file, got: {filepath}"
 5958: 
 5959:     ok, msg = SECURITY.validate_path(filepath)
 5960:     if not ok:
 5961:         return f"Error: {msg}"
 5962:     if not os.path.exists(filepath):
 5963:         return f"Error: notebook does not exist: {filepath}"
 5964: 
 5965:     try:
 5966:         with open(filepath, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
 5967:             nb = json.load(f)

 5969:         return f"Error: notebook is not valid JSON ({e})"
 5970:     except OSError as e:
 5971:         return f"Error: cannot read notebook ({e})"
 5972: 
 5973:     cells = nb.get("cells")
 5974:     if not isinstance(cells, list):
 5975:         return "Error: notebook structure invalid (cells not a list)"
 5976:     n = len(cells)
 5977: 
 5978:     if action == "insert":
 5979:         # cell_index == -1 (or >= n) = append
 5980:         if cell_index < 0 or cell_index > n:
 5981:             cell_index = n  # append

 6009:             return f"Error: cell_index {cell_index} out of bounds (0..{n - 1})"
 6010:         cells.pop(cell_index)

 6015:     # Codex review 2026-04-28: catch any Exception (json.dump can raise
 6016:     # TypeError on non-serialisable cell data, which is non-OSError) so the

 6033:

 6490:     def _cosine_similarity(self, a: List[float], b: List[float]) -> float:
 6491:         """Calculate cosine similarity between two vectors."""
 6492:         import numpy as np
 6493:         a_arr = np.array(a)
 6494:         b_arr = np.array(b)
 6495:         return float(np.dot(a_arr, b_arr) / (np.linalg.norm(a_arr) * np.linalg.norm(b_arr)))

 6497:     def index_codebase(self, root_dir: str, extensions: List[str] = None, chunk_size: int = 50) -> int:
 6498:         """Index all code files in directory."""
 6499:         extensions = extensions or [".py", ".js", ".ts", ".tsx", ".java", ".go", ".rs", ".c", ".cpp", ".h"]
 6500:         self.chunks = []
 6501: 
 6502:         for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root_dir):
 6503:             dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if not d.startswith(".")]
 6504:             for filename in filenames:
 6505:                 if not any(filename.endswith(ext) for ext in extensions):
 6506:                     continue
 6507:                 filepath = os.path.join(dirpath, filename)
 6508:                 self._index_file(filepath, chunk_size)
 6509: 
 6510:         self._save_index()
 6511:         return len(self.chunks)

 6513:     def _index_file(self, filepath: str, chunk_size: int = 50):
 6514:         """Split file into chunks and index each. Uses AST-based splitting for Python files."""
 6515:         try:
 6516:             with open(filepath, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
 6517:                 source = f.read()
 6518:         except IOError:
 6519:             return
 6520: 
 6521:         lines = source.split("\n")
 6522:         chunks = []
 6523: 
 6524:         # AST-based chunking for Python files â€” split by function/class
 6525:         if filepath.endswith(".py"):
 6526:             try:
 6527:                 import ast as _ast
 6528:                 tree = _ast.parse(source)
 6529:                 boundaries = []
 6530:                 for node in _ast.walk(tree):
 6531:                     if isinstance(node, (_ast.FunctionDef, _ast.AsyncFunctionDef, _ast.ClassDef)):
 6532:                         start = node.lineno - 1  # 0-indexed
 6533:                         end = node.end_lineno if hasattr(node, 'end_lineno') and node.end_lineno else start + 20
 6534:                         boundaries.append((start, end))
 6535:                 if boundaries:
 6536:                     # Sort by start line, merge overlapping
 6537:                     boundaries.sort()
 6538:                     merged = [boundaries[0]]
 6539:                     for s, e in boundaries[1:]:
 6540:                         if s <= merged[-1][1]:
 6541:                             merged[-1] = (merged[-1][0], max(merged[-1][1], e))
 6542:                         else:
 6543:                             merged.append((s, e))
 6544:                     for start, end in merged:
 6545:                         chunk_lines = lines[start:end]
 6546:                         content = "\n".join(chunk_lines)
 6547:                         if len(content.strip()) >= 50:
 6548:                             chunks.append((start + 1, end, content))
 6549:             except SyntaxError:
 6550:                 pass  # Fall through to line-based chunking
 6551: 
 6552:         # Fallback: fixed-size line chunks (for non-Python or if AST failed)
 6553:         if not chunks:
 6554:             for i in range(0, len(lines), chunk_size):
 6555:                 chunk_lines = lines[i:i + chunk_size]
 6556:                 content = "\n".join(chunk_lines)
 6557:                 if len(content.strip()) >= 50:
 6558:                     chunks.append((i + 1, i + len(chunk_lines), content))
 6559: 
 6560:         for start_line, end_line, content in chunks:
 6561:             try:
 6562:                 embedding = self._get_embedding(content)
 6563:                 self.chunks.append({
 6564:                     "file_path": filepath,
 6565:                     "start_line": start_line,
 6566:                     "end_line": end_line,
 6567:                     "content": content,
 6568:                     "embedding": embedding,
 6569:                 })
 6570:             except Exception as e:
 6571:                 print(f"Warning: Failed to embed {filepath}: {e}")
 6572: 
 6573:     def _save_index(self):
 6574:         """Save index to disk. No-op in stealth mode (keeps index in memory only)."""
 6575:         if CONFIG.disable_local_traces:
 6576:             return
 6577:         os.makedirs(self.index_path, exist_ok=True)
 6578:         with open(os.path.join(self.index_path, "chunks.json"), "w") as f:
 6579:             json.dump(self.chunks, f)
 6580: 
 6581:     def _load_index(self) -> bool:
 6582:         """Load index from disk."""
 6583:         path = os.path.join(self.index_path, "chunks.json")
 6584:         if not os.path.exists(path):
 6585:             return False
 6586:         try:
 6587:             with open(path) as f:
 6588:                 self.chunks = json.load(f)
 6589:             return True
 6590:         except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
 6591:             return False
 6592: 
 6593:     def search(self, query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> List[Tuple[Dict, float]]:
 6594:         """Search for code matching query."""
 6595:         if not self.chunks and not self._load_index():
 6596:             return []
 6597:         query_embedding = self._get_embedding(query)
 6598:         results = []
 6599:         for chunk in self.chunks:
 6600:             if chunk.get("embedding"):
 6601:                 sim = self._cosine_similarity(query_embedding, chunk["embedding"])
 6602:                 results.append((chunk, sim))
 6603:         results.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
 6604:         return results[:top_k]
 6605: 
 6606:     def is_indexed(self) -> bool:
 6607:         """Check if codebase is indexed."""
 6608:         return os.path.exists(os.path.join(self.index_path, "chunks.json"))

 6258: def _parse_markdown_table(text: str) -> list:
 6259:     """Parse markdown table into list of lists for PDF/reportlab."""
 6260:     lines = text.strip().split("\n")
 6261:     table_data = []
 6262:     for line in lines:
 6263:         stripped = line.strip()
 6264:         if not stripped:
 6265:             continue
 6266:         # Skip separator lines (all dashes/colons)
 6267:         if re.match(r'^[\|\s\-:]+$', stripped):
 6268:             continue
 6269:         # Parse table row
 6270:         if "|" in stripped:
 6271:             # Normalize: ensure leading/trailing | for consistent parsing
 6272:             if not stripped.startswith("|"):
 6273:                 stripped = "|" + stripped
 6274:             if not stripped.endswith("|"):
 6275:                 stripped = stripped + "|"
 6276:             cells = [c.strip() for c in stripped[1:-1].split("|")]
 6277:             if cells and any(c for c in cells):  # Skip empty rows
 6278:                 table_data.append(cells)
 6279:     return table_data

  24: _DESCRIPTION = """Writes content to a file, creating it if it doesn't exist or overwriting if it does.
  25: 
  26: Usage:
  27: - This tool will OVERWRITE the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
  28: - If this is an existing file, you MUST use read_file first to read its contents. This tool will error if you haven't read the file (prevents blind clobber).
  29: - Prefer edit_file for modifying existing files â€” it only sends the diff portion, saving tokens. Use write_file only for creating new files or complete rewrites.
  30: - Supports `mode='write'` (default â€” overwrites entire file) and `mode='append'` (adds to end). Append mode does NOT require a prior read.
  31: - The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path. Parent directories are created automatically.
  32: - Approval prompt shows colored before/after diff (green = added, red = removed) inline + click-to-expand-full-file (per V5_PLAN.md Phase 4).
  33: - Approval is required before the write happens.
  34: 
  35: WHEN to use:
  36: - Creating a brand-new file that doesn't exist yet
  37: - Complete rewrite of an existing file (after reading it first)
  38: - Appending content to the end of a file (mode='append')
  39: 
  40: WHEN NOT to use:
  41: - Modifying specific sections of an existing file â†’ use edit_file (cheaper, safer, fewer tokens)
  42: - Editing notebook cells â†’ use notebook_edit
  43: - Never use bash echo / heredoc / cat to write files â€” use this dedicated tool instead"""
  44:

  46: _INPUT_SCHEMA: Dict[str, Any] = {

  48:     "properties": {

  50:             "type": "string",
  51:             "description": "Absolute path to the file to write.",
  52:         },
  53:         "content": {
  54:             "type": "string",
  55:             "description": "Content to write.",
  56:         },
  57:         "mode": {
  58:             "type": "string",
  59:             "enum": ["write", "append"],
  60:             "description": "'write' (default) overwrites the entire file. 'append' adds to the end without requiring a prior read.",
  61:         },
  62:     },
  63:     "required": ["file_path", "content"],
  64: }
  65: 
  66: 
  67: def _write_file_executor(args: Dict[str, Any], context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> str:
  68:     file_path = args.get("file_path")
  69:     content = args.get("content")
  70:     mode = args.get("mode", "write")

**Findings**

- Critical: `web_fetch` drops both approval and SSRF protections. The new tool calls `requests.get()` directly and registers `requires_approval=False` at [web_fetch.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/web_fetch.py:65) and [web_fetch.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/web_fetch.py:95). In v5, approval only fires when that flag is true ([query_engine.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/core/query_engine.py:805)), while `web_fetch` is explicitly high-risk ([high_risk.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/security/high_risk.py:18)). v4 also blocked private/internal hosts, redirects, and capped reads at 2MB ([sagemaker_agent.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py:6799)). This is a security regression.

- Critical: all six document creators are unapproved filesystem writes and bypass workspace validation. `v4_documents.py` writes/saves directly to user-provided paths, e.g. [v4_documents.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/v4_documents.py:63), [v4_documents.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/v4_documents.py:147), [v4_documents.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/v4_documents.py:212), and registers them with `requires_approval=False` at [v4_documents.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/v4_documents.py:389). Existing mutating tools validate paths and require approval ([write_file.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/write_file.py:79), [write_file.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/write_file.py:140)); v4 document tools were also approval-gated ([sagemaker_agent.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py:7247)) and validated paths before writing ([sagemaker_agent.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py:5656).

- High: several “restored” tools do not preserve the advertised v4 input contracts, so v4-compatible calls can fail or produce wrong output. `create_excel` advertises `rows` and treats v4 `data=[{col: val}]` as scalar dict cells ([v4_documents.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/v4_documents.py:86), [v4_documents.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/v4_documents.py:100)) even though v4 advertised `data` list-of-dicts with chart columns ([sagemaker_agent.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py:7250). `create_chart` now expects label-value mappings ([v4_documents.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/v4_documents.py:250)) while v4 advertised `{labels: [], values: []}` and richer chart types ([sagemaker_agent.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py:7287). `create_pdf` reads `text`/`rows` fields ([v4_documents.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/v4_documents.py:313)) while v4 advertised `data` blocks ([sagemaker_agent.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py:7299)).

- Medium: non-document schemas also shrink the v4 advertised surface. `semantic_search` omits v4’s `status` action and uses `k` instead of `top_k` ([semantic_search.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/semantic_search.py:118), v4 at [sagemaker_agent.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py:7316)). `ask_user` omits optional `options` ([ask_user.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/ask_user.py:48), v4 at [sagemaker_agent.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py:7395)).

What looks correct: registration is idempotent via `_register()`/`find_tool_by_name`; the Block G3 test fix is valid; `create_html` is intentionally absent and locked by test. I could not run the tests locally because this shell only exposes the WindowsApps `python.exe` stub and it fails to execute.
